# LSTP QA Test Suite

Hardware-level regression tests for the LSTP host-and-device ecosystem. Pytest
exercises SPI, GPIO, IRQ, LED, I2C, UART, and IPMI interfaces that the Linux
driver exposes over USB, validating the host driver and attached LSTP devices
end-to-end against board YAML expectations.

A companion **wire suite** under [`wire/`](wire/) tests the LSTP protocol itself,
speaking to the device directly over USB bulk endpoints with no kernel driver in
the path. It covers what this suite structurally cannot reach — malformed frames,
short headers, bad lengths, reserved opcodes, config bounds — and shares the same
board YAML. See [`wire/README.md`](wire/README.md).

Please refer to the [LSTP Specification](docs/LSTP%20Specification%201.0%20--%2008-03-2026.pdf)
for details on the LSTP protocol. See [`LSTP-Enabled USB Hub`](docs/LSTP-Enabled%20USB%20Hub.pdf)
for the design document of a USB Hub with LSTP protocol support.

## Prerequisites

- **LSTP hardware** with the `lstp` kernel module loaded (`sudo modprobe lstp`).
  SPI tests also need spidev bound to flash CS lines (`auto_bind_spidev=1` on
  `modprobe`, or the suite binds via sysfs during setup).
- **Board config** in `boards/<name>.yaml` (see [Board configuration](#board-configuration)).
- **Python 3** virtual environment with packages from `requirements.txt`.
- **Elevated commands** — many tests run privileged operations through `sudo -n`
  in [`priv.py`](priv.py) (for example `modprobe`, `i2cdetect`, sysfs writes
  via `tee`, and `dmesg -r`). The test user needs a matching sudoers allowlist,
  or run pytest as root for local debugging.

## Quick start

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt

# Full suite (discovery + every configured domain + multichannel when applicable)
.venv/bin/pytest lstp_test.py -v --tb=short --board HELLOWORLD547

# Pin a specific USB interface (optional)
.venv/bin/pytest lstp_test.py -v --tb=short --board HELLOWORLD547 --usb-path 1-1:1.0

# Discovery plus one domain
.venv/bin/pytest lstp_test.py -v --tb=short --board HELLOWORLD547 --suite spi
```

### `--board`

Required. Selects `boards/<stem>.yaml`; matching is case-insensitive
(`boards/helloworld547.yaml` → `--board HELLOWORLD547`).

### `--usb-path` (optional)

Basename under `/sys/bus/usb/devices` (for example `1-1:1.0`). Use when more
than one LSTP interface matches the board `device_name`; otherwise the first
match is used.

### `--suite` (optional)

Omit for a full run (discovery plus every configured domain, and multichannel
when applicable). When set, discovery always runs, then the selected domain:

| `--suite` | Also runs |
|-----------|-----------|
| `spi` | SPI |
| `gpio` | GPIO |
| `irq` | GPIO and IRQ (IRQ loopback depends on GPIO direction checks passing first) |
| `led` | LED |
| `i2c` | I2C |
| `uart` | UART (the whole UART class is omitted when no device has both `console` and `baud` in YAML) |
| `ipmi` | IPMI module only (no test cases implemented yet) |

**Multichannel** is not a `--suite` value. During a full run, `test_multichannel`
runs when `multichannel.scaling_factor` is non-zero and at least two bandwidth
domains are active: `i2c.bandwidth`, GPIO lines tagged `gpio` (not `led`), or
`uart.devices.*.bandwidth`.

## How it fits together

- [`board_config.py`](board_config.py) loads `boards/*.yaml` (shared with wire/).
- [`lstp_test.py`](lstp_test.py) is the pytest entry point: thin `LstpTest*`
  collectors wrapping the `test_*.py` modules.
- [`conftest.py`](conftest.py) defines CLI options, session fixtures
  (`usb_sysfs`, `lstp_channels`, per-domain maps), and `--suite` filtering.
- [`test_*.py`](.) holds the test logic.
- [`device_results.py`](device_results.py) aggregates per-device pass/fail/skip
  into one result line per test; [`deviations.py`](deviations.py) maps board
  YAML `known_deviations` to xfails (shared with the wire suite).

Discovery selects the USB sysfs node where the `lstp` driver is bound and
`<usb>/lstp/name` matches the board YAML `device_name`. SPI master numbers,
gpiochip indices, and I2C bus numbers come from the live `lstp/channel/` walk,
not from hardcoded values in the tests.

## Board configuration

Add `boards/<stem>.yaml` and pass `--board <stem>`. The repo ships
[`boards/helloworld547.yaml`](boards/helloworld547.yaml) as a reference for the
[OpenSMA Helloworld547](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenSMA/tree/vr_sma/src/boards/mcxn547helloworld)
board (`--board HELLOWORLD547`).

Each file documents its schema in comments. Common top-level keys:

| Key | Role |
|-----|------|
| `device_name` | Must match `<usb>/lstp/name` |
| `expected_bcd_device` | Golden USB `bcdDevice` for the wire suite (`0` skips) |
| `known_deviations` | Per-target SADD waivers / open findings (see `deviations.py`) |
| `init` | Expected channel names by type (`spi`, `gpio`, `i2c`, `uart`, `ipmi`, `mmio`) |
| `spi` / `gpio` / `i2c` / `uart` / `ipmi` / `multichannel` | Domain expectations |

Use `[]`, `{}`, or `0` for empty sections, as noted in those comments.

## Test coverage

| Module | What it checks |
|--------|----------------|
| `test_discovery` | Driver loaded, USB bind and `device_name`, channel walk vs `init:` (including `mmio`), dmesg errors since connect |
| `test_spi` | SPI children, spidev bind/unbind, CS count, node access, flash JEDEC ID, sector erase/program/read, flash program/read bandwidth (`spi.bandwidth`) |
| `test_gpio` | Expected gpiochips, line count/names/directions, output toggle, read/write bandwidth |
| `test_irq` | GPIO loopback IRQ edges (`gpio.irq_loopback`) |
| `test_led` | LED devices from GPIO rows tagged `led`: node presence, required sysfs attrs, not requestable as GPIO, brightness set/clamp, timer blink, pattern clear/set/replace |
| `test_i2c` | Expected buses, `i2cdetect` (optional strict mode per bus), basic transaction paths, emulated SMBus block read (+ PEC), at24 EEPROM install/read/write, read bandwidth |
| `test_uart` | Loopback bandwidth and overflow recovery when `uart.devices.<name>` defines `console`, `baud`, and the optional `bandwidth` / `overflow` blocks |
| `test_ipmi` | Placeholder class only — no tests yet |
| `test_multichannel` | Concurrent I2C, GPIO, and UART bandwidth; each parallel result must meet the solo YAML floor times `multichannel.scaling_factor` |

### Protocol-level coverage

Driver-independent protocol tests live in the [`wire/`](wire/) suite (framing,
status codes, config bounds, negative cases, per-target deviation tracking). Run
it from this directory:

```sh
.venv/bin/pip install -r wire/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/pytest wire --board HELLOWORLD547 -m "not slow and not stress"
```

Note that the wire suite detaches the `lstp` driver while it runs, so re-bind the
interface before returning to `lstp_test.py`.

### Not yet covered

- LED sustained bandwidth measurements
- LED triggers beyond timer and hardware pattern (for example default-on, heartbeat)
- IPMI command/response through misc device nodes
- Automated device-tree overlay load/unload

Sources follow [PEP 8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/) with a 100-column limit.
Settings and scripts live under [`style/`](style/):

# LSTP Wire Test Suite

Protocol-level regression tests that speak LSTP directly over USB bulk endpoints
via libusb, with no kernel driver in the path. Where the parent suite asks "does
the driver expose working SPI/GPIO/I2C/UART interfaces?", these tests ask "does
the device implement the LSTP protocol as specified?" — framing, status codes,
config layout, bounds checking, ordering, and negative cases the driver would
never produce.

That difference is the reason the suite exists. A kernel driver never emits a
malformed frame, a short header, an over-declared length, or a reserved opcode,
so those paths are unreachable from the parent suite by construction.

## Relationship to the parent suite

|  | Parent suite (`../lstp_test.py`) | Wire suite (here) |
|--|----------------------------------|-------------------|
| Path to device | kernel `lstp` driver, then sysfs / `/dev` nodes | libusb bulk endpoints |
| Question answered | do the Linux interfaces work end to end | does the device obey the protocol |
| Needs the module loaded | yes | no — it detaches the driver while it runs |
| Malformed / negative frames | not reachable | core of the suite |

The two are complementary and share board YAML through
[`../board_config.py`](../board_config.py), so one file describes a part for both,
plus [`../device_results.py`](../device_results.py) (`DeviceRunner`) for
per-item pass/fail/skip tracking and [`../deviations.py`](../deviations.py)
for per-target `known_deviations` (most findings are exercised here; the driver
suite consults the same registry).

Running the wire suite detaches the kernel driver from the interface. Re-bind it
before running the parent suite again, for example:

```sh
echo -n "1-1.2.1:1.2" | sudo tee /sys/bus/usb/drivers/lstp/bind
```

## Prerequisites

- **LSTP hardware** reachable over USB. The kernel module does *not* need to be
  loaded; if it is, the suite detaches it for the duration of the run.
- **Board config** in `../boards/<name>.yaml` — the same files the parent suite
  uses, plus a few wire-only keys (see [Board configuration](#board-configuration)).
- **Python 3** virtual environment with [`requirements.txt`](requirements.txt)
  (pytest and pyusb, plus a libusb backend).
- **Device access.** Either run as root, or install a udev rule granting the test
  user access to the LSTP interface. A rule matching the vendor id and setting
  `MODE=0666` is enough, and is preferable to running the whole suite as root.

## Quick start

Run from the parent directory so the shared board loader resolves:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r wire/requirements.txt

# Everything except the long tiers -- the usual local run
.venv/bin/pytest wire --board HELLOWORLD547 -m "not slow and not stress"

# One module, verbose
.venv/bin/pytest wire/test_wire_config.py --board HELLOWORLD547 -v

# Full run including soak and stress (takes the SADD-mandated durations)
.venv/bin/pytest wire --board HELLOWORLD547

# Record what deviated, for the trackers
.venv/bin/pytest wire --board HELLOWORLD547 --deviations-report=wire-deviations.json
```

## Command-line options

| Option | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `--board <name>` | Selects `../boards/<stem>.yaml`, case-insensitively. Expected pins, buses, bandwidth floors, and declared deviations all come from it. |
| `--usb-path <PATH>` | sysfs basename (e.g. `1-1.2.1:1.2`) to pick one of several attached LSTP devices. With more than one present and no path given, the suite skips and lists the candidates rather than guessing. |
| `--wire-vid <HEX>` | Override the USB vendor id used to find the interface. |
| `--transport <name>` | Wire transport; `libusb` today. |
| `--target <name>` | Device under test (`real`; an emulated target arrives later). |
| `--allow-destructive` | Opt in to tests that mutate persistent or one-time-programmable state. Off by default, so a normal run cannot brick a part. |
| `--allow-i2c-data-path` | Force I2C bus-transaction tests to run on a firmware revision known to hang the link on any I2C transfer. |
| `--uart-loopback-raw` | Assert the UART TX/RX pair is a true hardware short. Without it, UART tests assume a console peer and stay printable-safe. |
| `--stress-iters <N>` | Iteration count for stress/soak/fuzz tests (default 200). |
| `--soak-seconds <S>` | Wall-clock duration for the `soak` profile of parametrized soak tests. |
| `--soak-cycles <N>` | Cycle count for the `soak` profile of reset cycling. |
| `--deviations-report <PATH>` | Write this run's per-finding deviation record as JSON. |

## Test tiers

Markers select how much of the suite runs:

| Marker | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `slow` | Long-running soak tests; nightly rather than per-commit. |
| `stress` | High-volume stress and fuzz tests. |
| `destructive` | Mutates persistent or OTP state; additionally gated by `--allow-destructive`. |
| `transport(name)` | The wire transport a test targets. |
| `target(name)` | The device type a test targets. |
| `faults` | Device-to-host fault injection; needs the emulated target. |

Tests that exist in both a fast and a full form are parametrized `[smoke]` and
`[soak]`, so `-m "not slow"` keeps the smoke variant and drops the soak one.

## Known deviations

The suite **always asserts specification-correct behaviour**. It never softens an
assertion because a particular part misbehaves. Instead, when a test observes a
deviation it consults a per-target registry ([`../deviations.py`](../deviations.py)) to
decide the verdict:

| Situation | Verdict |
|-----------|---------|
| The board YAML declares this finding | `xfail`, naming the finding and its disposition |
| It does not declare it | **hard failure** — a new defect, or a part inheriting another part's quirk |
| Declared, but observing it damages the device | `xfail` without touching the device |

The point is regression control. A blanket `xfail` written for one part silently
excuses the same bug on every other part and can never fail again; declaring
deviations per target makes each board file an explicit, reviewable compliance
record, and keeps a fresh firmware bug from hiding inside a green-looking xfail.

### Declaring a deviation

In `../boards/<name>.yaml`:

```yaml
known_deviations:
  F12:
    status: open        # an open defect; xfail only so it does not block CI
    note: "partial config writes are ACKed but never latch"
    ticket: LSTP-1234   # optional
  F3:
    status: accepted    # a reviewed, deliberate waiver for this part
    note: "MMIO config is read-only by design here"
```

A bare string (`F12: "note"`) or a plain list (`known_deviations: [F1, F2]`) also
works and means `status: open`, which is the right default while a part is still
being stabilised.

The key is a finding id, and it must match the one the deviation site names in its
`finding <ID>: ...` message — that phrase is how the id is parsed, which is also
why a message may mention requirement ids of the same shape (`GPIO-013`) without
being mistaken for one. `F<n>` ids are shared protocol-stack findings that any part
can exhibit; a deviation seen on only one part is better given a target-qualified
id (`MYBOARD-1`) so it cannot be confused with an unrelated finding elsewhere.

`open` and `accepted` both xfail, so neither blocks CI. They differ in what they
assert and in their exit criteria:

- **open** — this is broken and expected to be fixed. The declaration is a
  temporary loan against a real defect and should be deleted once the fix lands.
- **accepted** — reviewed and waived for this part. It stays.

### Reading a run

Every run ends with the deviation ledger:

```text
=================== LSTP deviations: <board> ===================
  F1    open        seen      bulk-OUT spanning >1 USB max packet is framed per ...
  F3    accepted    not seen  MMIO config is read-only by design on this part ...
  totals: 15 open defect(s) xfailed, 2 accepted waiver(s), 0 undeclared
  never reproduced this run: F3, F10 -- either the covering test did not run
  (marker/layout skip), or the device no longer deviates and the declaration
  should be deleted
```

`not seen` is a warning, never a failure: the covering test may simply have been
filtered out by a marker or skipped for the layout. But on a full run it is the
signal that a declaration has outlived its defect and should go.

### Workflows

**A run reports an undeclared deviation.** Treat it as a new finding. Reproduce
it, raise it, then either fix the device or declare it `open` with a ticket. Do
not declare it just to green the run — that is what the failure is protecting
against.

**A declared deviation stops reproducing.** The ledger lists it under "never
reproduced". Confirm the covering test actually ran, then delete the declaration
so the test goes green and any regression fails loudly again.

**Observing a deviation damages the device.** Some defects cannot be probed
safely — a flag toggle that wedges a bus, or a command that hangs the firmware
until a power cycle. Those sites call `deviations.unsafe_to_probe(fid, ...)`,
which xfails without issuing the damaging request when the target declares the
finding, and otherwise lets the real check run so a fixed part can prove it.

## Board configuration

The wire suite reads the same `../boards/<name>.yaml` files as the parent suite
and adds a few keys of its own:

| Key | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| `expected_bcd_device` | Golden USB `bcdDevice` for the programmed image, checked as a manufacturing trace. |
| `known_deviations` | This part's declared deviations (above). |
| `i2c.smbus` | Declares a true SMBus-block-capable target. SMBus compliance tests skip without it, because an EEPROM cannot answer the question. |
| `UNSAFE_ignore_write_config_mode_result` | Lets config-write tests proceed on firmware with no to-RAM config mode. Writes may then reach non-volatile storage — opt in deliberately. |

Pins, buses, addresses, and bandwidth floors come from the shared sections, so
per-part expectations live in one file rather than in the tests.

## Test coverage

| Module | What it checks |
|--------|----------------|
| `test_wire_discovery` | Interface descriptors, LSTP version, channel enumeration, per-channel descriptors, manufacturing trace |
| `test_wire_config` | ch0 `READ_CONFIG` / `WRITE_CONFIG`: offsets, bounds, chunked reassembly, config modes, descriptor and flag writes, channel enable/disable, config lock, serviceability sweeps |
| `test_wire_protocol` | Framing, header validation, short and over-declared lengths, reserved opcodes, ordering, bulk packing, status mapping, USB reset recovery |
| `test_wire_spi` | Config prefix validity, full-duplex transfer, chip-select selection and hold, idle reads, unknown opcodes, posted writes |
| `test_wire_gpio` | Pin table, directions, values, config-field writes, debounce, IRQ config and events, LED pattern policy, reset defaults |
| `test_wire_i2c` | Config and speeds, target presence and NACK behaviour, EEPROM integrity, length bounds, bus recovery, SMBus block reads and PEC |
| `test_wire_uart` | Config and baud rates, data bits, flow-control policy, loopback patterns, RX burst handling, break generation, soak |
| `test_wire_multichannel` | Concurrent multi-channel traffic, isolation, status reporting, full service sequences |
| `test_wire_stress` | Latency benchmarks, concurrency and ordering under load, fuzz and soak profiles |

## How it fits together

- [`transport.py`](transport.py) — L1: interface discovery, bulk I/O, reset and
  re-enumeration.
- [`lstp_proto.py`](lstp_proto.py) — L0: header build/parse, status and enum
  definitions, protocol constants.
- [`ops/`](ops) — L2: per-subsystem request builders and decoders (`ch0`, `gpio`,
  `i2c`, `uart`, `spi`, `mmio`).
- [`mux.py`](mux.py) — thread-safe channel multiplexer that demultiplexes
  responses from unsolicited events for concurrency tests.
- [`softloop.py`](softloop.py) — safe UART exchange against a console peer, for
  rigs with no true hardware loopback.
- [`helpers.py`](helpers.py) — shared assertions used across wire tests.
- [`../deviations.py`](../deviations.py) — the per-target deviation registry
  (shared with the driver suite).
- [`../board_config.py`](../board_config.py) / [`../device_results.py`](../device_results.py)
  — shared board YAML loader and per-item result aggregation.
- [`conftest.py`](conftest.py) — CLI options, session fixtures, safety gates, and
  the deviation ledger.

# Phase 1 end-to-end slice: claim the interface over libusb and enumerate the
# device via ch0 READ_CONFIG, entirely bypassing the kernel driver. Proves the
# claim/detach lifecycle, the transport, and the protocol/ops stack against a
# real device. Deeper functional-over-wire suites (gpio/i2c/uart/spi) build on
# this in later phases.

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings

import pytest

import lstp_proto as proto
from ops import ch0

pytestmark = pytest.mark.transport("libusb")


# init-list key -> channel type it should enumerate as.
_NAME_TYPE_KEYS = {
    "spi": proto.ChannelType.SPI,
    "gpio": proto.ChannelType.GPIO,
    "i2c": proto.ChannelType.I2C,
    "uart": proto.ChannelType.UART,
    "ipmi": proto.ChannelType.IPMI,
    "mmio": proto.ChannelType.MMIO,
}

# Fallback tag per channel type, used only when a channel reports an empty raw
# name (the enumerated name then falls back to "<intf>_<TAG>_CH<id>").
_CH_TYPE_TAGS = {
    proto.ChannelType.SPI: "SPI",
    proto.ChannelType.GPIO: "GPIO",
    proto.ChannelType.I2C: "I2C",
    proto.ChannelType.UART: "UART",
    proto.ChannelType.IPMI: "IPMI",
    proto.ChannelType.MMIO: "MMIO",
}


def _display_name(intf_name: str, ch) -> str:
    """Promote a raw ch0 channel to its enumerated ``<intf>_<ch>`` name.

    The board YAMLs list the enumerated channel names (``<intf>_<ch>``, or
    ``<intf>_<TAG>_CH<id>`` when the firmware name is empty), while ch0 reports
    the raw firmware name; build the same form here so the wire suite can
    consume the shared board defs.
    """
    if ch.name:
        return f"{intf_name}_{ch.name}"
    tag = _CH_TYPE_TAGS.get(ch.ch_type, "UNKNOWN")
    return f"{intf_name}_{tag}_CH{ch.ch_id}"


def _expected_name_types(board_cfg: dict) -> dict[str, proto.ChannelType | None]:
    init = board_cfg.get("init", {})
    out: dict[str, proto.ChannelType | None] = {}
    for key, ch_type in _NAME_TYPE_KEYS.items():
        for name in init.get(key, []):
            out[name] = ch_type
    return out

    def test_mgmt_read_payload_length(self, wire_transport):
        """DISC-004: the management READ_CONFIG response's length field is exact.

        The management config read carries a header payload-length field; assert
        it equals the bytes actually delivered (no truncation, no padding) and is
        large enough to cover the descriptor head plus the ch0 config, then that
        the declared span parses into a self-consistent ch0 config. This closes
        the "payload length field not asserted" gap on the descriptor read.
        """
        length = ch0.max_config_len(wire_transport)
        req = proto.pack_ch0_read_req(0, 0, length)
        wire_transport.drain(timeout_ms=50)
        wire_transport.send_raw(proto.build_request(0, proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG, req))
        frame = wire_transport.recv_raw()
        hdr = proto.parse_header(frame)
        # Some firmware rejects the explicit per-packet max; fall back to the
        # documented deprecated length=0 form, exactly as ops.ch0.read_config does.
        if not (hdr.is_response and hdr.code == proto.Status.SUCCESS):
            req = proto.pack_ch0_read_req(0, 0, proto.DEPRECATED_READ_CONFIG_MAX)
            wire_transport.drain(timeout_ms=50)
            wire_transport.send_raw(proto.build_request(0, proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG, req))
            frame = wire_transport.recv_raw()
            hdr = proto.parse_header(frame)

        assert hdr.is_response, "management READ_CONFIG did not return a response frame"
        assert hdr.code == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
            f"management READ_CONFIG -> {proto.Status(hdr.code).name}"
        )
        body = frame[proto.HEADER_SIZE :]
        assert hdr.length == len(body), (
            f"declared payload length {hdr.length} != delivered {len(body)} bytes"
        )
        min_len = proto.CH0_READ_RESP_HEAD_SIZE + proto.CH0_CONFIG_SIZE
        assert hdr.length >= min_len, (
            f"declared payload length {hdr.length} < mgmt head+config {min_len}"
        )
        cfg = proto.parse_ch0_config(body[proto.CH0_READ_RESP_HEAD_SIZE :])
        assert cfg.lstp_version == proto.LSTP_VERSION
        assert 1 <= cfg.num_channels < proto.MAX_CHANNELS

        gpio_dev = (board_cfg.get("gpio") or {}).get("devices") or {}

        for _label, lines in gpio_dev.items():

                        continue
                    if pin.name != name:
                        problems.append(f"GPIO offset {off}: name {pin.name!r} != board {name!r}")
                    if want_dir in ("input", "output"):

                        if dev_dir != want_dir:

                            )

        # UART: decoded speed vs YAML baud.
        uart_dev = (board_cfg.get("uart") or {}).get("devices") or {}
        want_baud = None
        for _name, spec in uart_dev.items():

def _read_frame(target_ch: int) -> bytes:
    req = proto.pack_ch0_read_req(target_ch, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
    return proto.build_request(0, proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG, req)


def _i2c_present_absent(board_cfg):
    """Return ``(present_addr, absent_addr)`` from board YAML, or ``(None, None)``.

    A non-skipping counterpart to the ``i2c_targets`` fixture, for stress tests
    that must still run on boards without I2C rather than skip entirely. Prefers
    an EEPROM (ACKs a bare read) as the present target.
    """
    i2c_cfg = (board_cfg or {}).get("i2c") or {}
    devices = i2c_cfg.get("devices") or {}
    addrs = sorted({int(a) for lst in devices.values() for a in lst})
    if not addrs:
        return None, None
    eeprom: dict[int, list] = {}
    for bus_map in (i2c_cfg.get("i2c_eeprom") or {}).values():
        for addr in bus_map:
            eeprom[int(addr)] = True
    present = sorted(eeprom)[0] if eeprom else addrs[0]
    absent = next((a for a in range(0x10, 0x78) if a not in addrs), None)
    return present, absent


def _first_readable_gpio(transport, discovery):
    """Return ``(gpio_channel, pin_index)`` for a non-LED pin, or ``(ch|None, None)``.

    Reads the GPIO config *through the given transport* (so it works via the
    mux), giving concurrency tests a second real channel id to drive alongside
    ch0. Returns ``(None, None)`` when the layout has no GPIO channel.
    """
    gch = next((c for c in discovery.channels if c.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.GPIO), None)
    if gch is None:
        return None, None
    try:
        cfg = gpio.read_gpio_config(transport, gch.ch_id)
    except (proto.LstpStatusError, proto.LstpProtocolError):
        return gch, None
    pins = [p.index for p in cfg.pins if not p.config.is_led]
    return gch, (pins[0] if pins else None)

    def test_same_channel_in_order(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """MLTI-003: serialized ch0 reads each return the requested channel's desc.

        LSTP serializes requests per channel id (one outstanding at a time), so
        this issues each ch0 read and consumes its reply before the next, and
        checks the reply describes the channel that was asked for.

            desc = proto.parse_ch_desc(resp[proto.HEADER_SIZE :])

            )

def _pct(sorted_ms: list[float], p: float) -> float:
    """Nearest-rank percentile on an already-sorted sample list."""
    idx = min(len(sorted_ms) - 1, max(0, round(p / 100 * len(sorted_ms)) - 1))
    return sorted_ms[idx]


def _emit_latency(label: str, sorted_ms: list[float]) -> None:
    """Print one latency distribution line for the bring-up log (no assert).

    Reports n / mean / p50 / p95 / p99 / max (ms) plus an advisory OK/OVER flag
    against the policy median target and the hard transport timeout. The
    STRS-005 benchmarks *record* the distribution rather than gate pass/fail, so
    the numbers always print (run with ``-s`` or ``-rP`` to surface them) and
    nothing is asserted.
    """
    mean = statistics.fmean(sorted_ms)
    p50, p95, p99, mx = (
        _pct(sorted_ms, 50),
        _pct(sorted_ms, 95),
        _pct(sorted_ms, 99),
        sorted_ms[-1],
    )
    adv = (
        f"p50<{proto.LSTP_LATENCY_TARGET_MS}:"
        f"{'ok' if p50 < proto.LSTP_LATENCY_TARGET_MS else 'OVER'} "
        f"p99<{proto.USB_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS}:"
        f"{'ok' if p99 < proto.USB_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS else 'OVER'}"
    )
    print(
        f"[STRS-005] {label:22s} n={len(sorted_ms):3d} mean={mean:6.2f} "
        f"p50={p50:6.2f} p95={p95:6.2f} p99={p99:6.2f} max={mx:6.2f} ms  ({adv})"
    )


class TestConcurrentMux:
    """Threaded, channel-multiplexed concurrency over the wire (MLTI-003/005,
    MGMT-005, STRS-005/006).

    Uses the ``wire_mux`` fixture: one background reader demultiplexes bulk-IN by
    channel id while worker threads each hold one in-flight request per channel.
    This is what actually exercises LSTP's per-channel concurrency model -- the
    serialized tests in :class:`TestConcurrency` can only prove ordering.
    """

    def test_same_channel_concurrent(self, wire_mux):
        """MLTI-003: many host threads contend on the *same* channel (ch0).

        The mux serializes them per the one-outstanding-per-channel contract; the
        assertion is that every reply is a valid, correctly-routed ch0 descriptor
        and the total reply count matches the requests -- i.e. no lost, duplicated,
        or cross-talked responses under same-channel contention.
        """
        n_threads, per = 6, 15

        def worker() -> int:
            for _ in range(per):
                res = ch0.read_config(wire_mux, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
                assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT
            return per

        with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=n_threads) as ex:
            totals = [f.result() for f in [ex.submit(worker) for _ in range(n_threads)]]
        assert sum(totals) == n_threads * per

    def test_interleaved_channels_concurrent(self, wire_mux, wire_discovery):
        """MLTI-005: threads drive *distinct* channels concurrently (ch0 + GPIO).

        Proves no cross-channel corruption: ch0 replies always decode as a full
        MGMT descriptor, and GPIO GET_VALUE replies are always a single 0/1 byte.
        A misrouted or payload-corrupted frame (e.g. a ch0-sized reply delivered
        to the GPIO waiter) would fail the per-channel shape check.
        """
        gch, pin = _first_readable_gpio(wire_mux, wire_discovery)
        if gch is None or pin is None:
            pytest.skip("need a GPIO channel + readable pin for a 2nd concurrent channel")
        per = 20

        def ch0_worker() -> int:
            for _ in range(per):
                res = ch0.read_config(wire_mux, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
                assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT
                assert res.config, "ch0 reply missing config body"
            return per

        def gpio_worker() -> int:
            req = struct.pack("<H", pin & 0xFFFF)
            for _ in range(per):
                status, body = wire_mux.request(
                    gch.ch_id, gpio.GpioCmd.GET_VALUE, req, raise_on_error=False
                )
                assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS
                assert len(body) == 1 and body[0] in (0, 1), (
                    f"GPIO reply not a 1-byte value (cross-channel corruption?): {body.hex()}"
                )
            return per

        with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as ex:
            futs = [
                ex.submit(ch0_worker),
                ex.submit(gpio_worker),
                ex.submit(ch0_worker),
                ex.submit(gpio_worker),
            ]
            done = [f.result() for f in futs]
        assert sum(done) == 4 * per

    def test_latency_under_load(self, wire_mux, wire_discovery, stress_iters):
        """STRS-005 (under-load): ch0 latency while other channels run traffic.

        Complements the idle `test_idle_latency`: measures ch0 round-trip latency
        with background GPIO threads saturating a second channel. This is a
        benchmark: it prints both the idle baseline and the under-load
        distribution (with an advisory OK/OVER flag against the
        ``LSTP_LATENCY_TARGET_MS`` (100 ms) policy target and the transport
        timeout) for the bring-up log, and does not assert.
        """
        import transport as tr

        gch, pin = _first_readable_gpio(wire_mux, wire_discovery)
        if gch is None or pin is None:
            pytest.skip("need a GPIO channel + readable pin to generate background load")
        n = max(20, min(stress_iters, 300))

        def measure() -> list[float]:
            samples: list[float] = []
            for _ in range(n):
                start = time.monotonic()
                ch0.read_config(wire_mux, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
                samples.append((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
            samples.sort()
            return samples

        idle = measure()

        stop = threading.Event()

        def bg() -> None:
            req = struct.pack("<H", pin & 0xFFFF)
            while not stop.is_set():
                try:
                    wire_mux.request(gch.ch_id, gpio.GpioCmd.GET_VALUE, req, raise_on_error=False)
                except (tr.TransportError, proto.LstpProtocolError):
                    break

        threads = [threading.Thread(target=bg, daemon=True) for _ in range(2)]
        for th in threads:
            th.start()
        try:
            load = measure()
        finally:
            stop.set()
            for th in threads:
                th.join(timeout=2.0)
        alive = [t for t in threads if t.is_alive()]
        assert not alive, (
            f"{len(alive)} background load worker(s) still running after stop; "
            "a stuck worker would keep using wire_mux after teardown"
        )

        _emit_latency("idle ch0", idle)
        _emit_latency("under-load ch0", load)

            got = 0
            for _ in range(n):
                _st, data = i2c.request_read(wire_mux, ich.ch_id, i2c_addr, i2c_rb)
                got += len(data)
            return got  # bytes

        uch = next(
            (c for c in wire_discovery.channels if c.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.UART), None
        )
        u_n = max(10, n // 8)  # UART round-trips are serial-rate; fewer iters

        def uart_worker() -> int:
            got = 0
            for i in range(u_n):
                echoed = softloop.mux_soft_loopback(
                    wire_mux, uch.ch_id, softloop.printable(8, seed=i)
                )
                got += len(echoed)
            return got  # bytes

        # Build the concurrent workload; capture each channel's own rate.
        jobs: dict[str, callable] = {"ch0": ch0_worker}
        if gch is not None and pin is not None:
            jobs["gpio"] = gpio_worker
        # The I2C leg is dropped (not skipped) when the firmware's I2C data path
        # would wedge the link (finding F21), so the remaining channels still get
        # their aggregate figures.
        if ich is not None and i2c_present is not None and i2c_data_path_ok:
            jobs["i2c"] = i2c_worker
        if uch is not None:
            jobs["uart"] = uart_worker

        with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(jobs)) as ex:
            futs = {name: ex.submit(timed, fn) for name, fn in jobs.items()}
            for name, fut in futs.items():
                results[name] = fut.result()
        if uch is not None:
            softloop.mux_clear_line(wire_mux, uch.ch_id)

        for name, rate in results.items():
            unit = "ops/s" if name in ("ch0", "gpio") else "B/s"
            report.append(f"{name}={rate:.0f}{unit}")

        # Non-starvation is the hard wire-scope assertion: with every channel
        # contending on the one bulk pipe, none may be shut out -- each must make
        # real forward progress rather than being starved by the others.
        assert results, "no channels available to measure aggregate throughput"
        assert all(r > 1 for r in results.values()), (
            f"a channel was starved under aggregate load ({report})"
        )

        # Product per-channel floors (scaled) are asserted against the board YAML,
        # but they are a *driver-path* target (parallel kernel URBs). The wire
        # path multiplexes every channel over a single Python-driven bulk pipe
        # with one demux reader, so aggregate per-channel throughput is round-trip
        # bound and structurally cannot reach the product floor (finding F15). The
        # absolute floors are enforced solo instead (see test_gpio_throughput /
        # test_per_class_latency). Keep the spec-correct assertion and xfail the
        # wire-mux shortfall so the product target stays visible in the tracker.
        shortfalls: list[str] = []
        gpio_floor = TestGpio.min_ops_per_s(board_cfg) if board_cfg else 0
        if "gpio" in results and gpio_floor and results["gpio"] < gpio_floor * scale:
            shortfalls.append(f"GPIO {results['gpio']:.0f} < {gpio_floor} x {scale} ops/s")
        if "i2c" in results and i2c_case and results["i2c"] < i2c_case[1] * scale:
            shortfalls.append(
                f"I2C {results['i2c']:.0f} < {i2c_case[1]} x {scale} B/s ({i2c_rb}-byte reads)"
            )
        if shortfalls:
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F15: wire-mux aggregate per-channel throughput below the "
                "product floor (single shared bulk pipe, round-trip bound): "
                f"{shortfalls}; product per-channel bandwidth is validated solo "
                f"and on the driver path. Full report: {report}"
            )


class TestSoak:
    """Valid-random packet fuzz and service repeatability (STRS-004, RAS-001)."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "profile", ["smoke", pytest.param("soak", marks=[pytest.mark.slow, pytest.mark.stress])]
    )
    def test_packet_fuzz_soak(
        self,
        wire_transport,
        wire_discovery,
        board_cfg,
        profile,
        soak_seconds,
        i2c_data_path_ok,
        volatile_writes,
    ):
        """STRS-004: valid-random traffic across commands + channels keeps the device
        synced (no crash, only defined statuses).

        Broadened beyond ch0 reads: each iteration randomly picks one of the
        available *well-formed* actions -- ch0 READ_CONFIG (valid + out-of-range),
        an *idempotent* ch0 WRITE_CONFIG (the channel's own descriptor written
        back), GPIO GET_VALUE / GET_IRQ_CONFIG on a random valid pin, I2C reads
        (present + absent target), and safe UART soft-loopback writes. Every
        action must return a defined LSTP status and the link must still be synced
        at the end. Only read / idempotent / non-CR-submitting actions are used,
        so the soak cannot mutate persistent state nor reach the console login.

        Two profiles: ``smoke`` (default, unconditional) runs a short fixed number
        of iterations; ``soak`` (marked slow+stress) runs for the full SADD
        1-hour duration (or ``--soak-seconds``). Every wire-observable STRS-004
        clause (no crash, only defined statuses, still synced) is covered; the
        "no kernel memory leak" clause stays in the driver suite.
        """
        rng = random.Random(0xF0F0)
        max_ch = wire_discovery.num_channels
        cap = ch0.max_config_len(wire_transport)

        def _assert_defined(status: int) -> None:
            assert status in tuple(proto.Status), f"undefined status 0x{status:02x}"

        def act_valid_read() -> None:
            target = rng.randint(0, max_ch)
            status, _ = ch0.request_read_config(
                wire_transport, target, rng.randint(0, 8), rng.randint(1, cap)
            )
            _assert_defined(status)

        def act_oob_read() -> None:
            bad = max_ch + rng.randint(1, 100)
            status, _ = ch0.request_read_config(wire_transport, bad, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
            assert status != proto.Status.SUCCESS

        # Reads are weighted heaviest; extra action types appended when available.
        actions = [act_valid_read, act_valid_read, act_oob_read]

        writable = next(
            (
                c
                for c in wire_discovery.channels
                if ch0.supports_desc_write(wire_transport, c.ch_id)
            ),
            None,
        )
        if writable is not None:

            def act_idempotent_write() -> None:
                cur = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, writable.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
                status, _ = ch0.write_desc(
                    wire_transport,
                    writable.ch_id,
                    0,
                    cur.desc.ch_type,
                    cur.desc.ch_flags,
                    cur.desc.ch_name,
                    raise_on_error=False,
                )
                _assert_defined(status)

            actions.append(act_idempotent_write)

        gch = next(
            (c for c in wire_discovery.channels if c.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.GPIO), None
        )
        gpins: list[int] = []
        if gch is not None:
            try:
                gcfg = gpio.read_gpio_config(wire_transport, gch.ch_id)
                gpins = [p.index for p in gcfg.pins if not p.config.is_led]
            except (proto.LstpStatusError, proto.LstpProtocolError):
                gpins = []
        if gpins:

            def act_gpio_read() -> None:
                pin = struct.pack("<H", rng.choice(gpins) & 0xFFFF)
                cmd = rng.choice((gpio.GpioCmd.GET_VALUE, gpio.GpioCmd.GET_IRQ_CONFIG))
                status, _ = wire_transport.request(gch.ch_id, cmd, pin, raise_on_error=False)
                _assert_defined(status)

            actions.append(act_gpio_read)

        ich = next((c for c in wire_discovery.channels if c.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.I2C), None)
        i2c_present, i2c_absent = _i2c_present_absent(board_cfg)
        # I2C reads are left out of the action mix when the firmware's I2C data
        # path would wedge the link (finding F21): the fuzzer would hit it within
        # a few iterations and kill the rest of the soak.
        if ich is not None and i2c_present is not None and i2c_data_path_ok:
            i2c_cap = wire_transport.bulk_rx_size - proto.HEADER_SIZE

            def act_i2c_read() -> None:
                addr = rng.choice([a for a in (i2c_present, i2c_absent) if a is not None])
                status, _ = i2c.request_read(
                    wire_transport, ich.ch_id, addr, rng.randint(1, i2c_cap)
                )
                _assert_defined(status)

            actions.append(act_i2c_read)

        uch = next(
            (c for c in wire_discovery.channels if c.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.UART), None
        )
        if uch is not None:

            def act_uart_write() -> None:
                # Printable, newline-free payload -- never submits to the console
                # login. Drain+ack the echo so the next action reads its own reply.
                payload = softloop.printable(rng.randint(1, 32), seed=rng.randint(0, 93))
                status, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, uch.ch_id, payload)
                _assert_defined(status)
                softloop.flush_rx(wire_transport, uch.ch_id, quiet_ms=80, max_ms=1200)

            actions.append(act_uart_write)

        def _step() -> None:
            # This rig's UART is a getty console, so a UART write's echo is an
            # *asynchronous* unsolicited RX frame that can land past its flush
            # window and, on the shared bulk-IN pipe, be misread as the next
            # action's response (desync: "expected response, got raw 0x00").
            # Drain any such residual before each action reads its own reply --
            # exactly the unsolicited-traffic case transport.drain() exists for.
            wire_transport.drain()
            rng.choice(actions)()

        if profile == "soak":
            deadline = time.monotonic() + (soak_seconds or _STRS004_SOAK_SECONDS)
            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                _step()
        else:
            for _ in range(_STRS004_SMOKE_ITERS):
                _step()
        # Leave the console line clean if we touched UART, then drain any last
        # unsolicited echo so the closing sync read (and fixture teardown) start
        # from an empty pipe.
        if uch is not None:
            softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, uch.ch_id)
        wire_transport.drain()
        # Still synced at the end.
        assert ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX).config

    def test_service_check_repeatable(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """RAS-001: the full discovery/service sequence is byte-for-byte repeatable.

        Snapshots the complete service-visible state -- device bcdDevice, LSTP
        version, interface name, channel count, and every channel's (id, type,
        name, enabled) -- and asserts it is identical across several repeats, not
        just twice, so a single consistent pair cannot pass it.
        """
        reps = 5

        def snapshot():
            disc = ch0.discover(wire_transport)
            return (
                wire_transport.bcd_device,
                disc.lstp_version,
                disc.intf_name,
                disc.num_channels,
                tuple((c.ch_id, c.ch_type, c.name, c.enabled) for c in disc.channels),
            )

        first = snapshot()
        for i in range(1, reps):
            assert snapshot() == first, f"service snapshot changed on repeat {i}"

from __future__ import annotations

import statistics
import time

import pytest

import helpers
import deviations

pytestmark = pytest.mark.transport("libusb")

# STRS-002 reset cycling: SADD specifies 500 cycles. Re-enumeration is slow
# (seconds each), so the default ('smoke') profile does a small fixed count and
# the 'soak' profile (marked slow+stress) runs the full SADD count (or
# --soak-cycles when set).
_STRS002_SOAK_CYCLES = 500
_STRS002_SMOKE_CYCLES = 3


def _ch0_read_frame(target_ch: int = 0) -> bytes:
    """A well-formed ch0 READ_CONFIG request for *target_ch*'s config."""
    req = proto.pack_ch0_read_req(target_ch, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
    return proto.build_request(0, proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG, req)


def _valid_ch0_read_frame() -> bytes:
    """A well-formed ch0 READ_CONFIG request for ch0's own config."""
    return _ch0_read_frame(0)


def _assert_still_synced(wire_transport):
    """A valid ch0 read must still work (proves no desync)."""
    wire_transport.drain()
    res = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
    assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT


class TestFraming:
    """Header encode/decode and basic framing (MGMT-001)."""

    def test_response_header_shape(self, wire_transport):
        """MGMT-001: response is a 4-byte LE header, response bit set, len matches."""
        wire_transport.send_raw(_valid_ch0_read_frame())
        resp = wire_transport.recv_raw()
        assert len(resp) >= proto.HEADER_SIZE
        hdr = proto.parse_header(resp)
        assert hdr.is_response, "response bit (7) not set on reply"
        assert hdr.ch_id == 0
        assert hdr.code == proto.Status.SUCCESS
        body = resp[proto.HEADER_SIZE :]
        assert len(body) >= hdr.length, "declared length exceeds bytes returned"

    def test_length_is_little_endian(self, wire_transport):
        """MGMT-001: the header length field decodes as little-endian u16."""
        wire_transport.send_raw(_valid_ch0_read_frame())
        resp = wire_transport.recv_raw()
        raw_len = resp[2] | (resp[3] << 8)
        assert proto.parse_header(resp).length == raw_len


class TestOrderingAndBackpressure:
    """Sequential processing and overload behavior (MGMT-004/005/006)."""

    def test_sequential_ordering(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """MGMT-004: serialized requests each get their *own* reply, matched by content.

        LSTP serializes requests per channel id (one outstanding at a time). To
        prove each reply belongs to its request -- not merely that "a response
        arrived" -- every read targets a *distinct* channel and the reply's
        descriptor type is checked against the channel that was asked for. A run
        of identical ch0 reads could not detect a stale or swapped reply; a
        sequence of distinct targets can.
        """
        targets = [0] + [c.ch_id for c in wire_discovery.channels]
        expected = [proto.ChannelType.MGMT] + [c.ch_type for c in wire_discovery.channels]
        wire_transport.drain()
        for target, want_type in zip(targets, expected):
            wire_transport.send_raw(_ch0_read_frame(target))
            resp = wire_transport.recv_raw()
            hdr = proto.parse_header(resp)
            assert hdr.is_response and hdr.ch_id == 0
            assert hdr.code == proto.Status.SUCCESS
            desc = proto.parse_ch_desc(resp[proto.HEADER_SIZE :])
            assert desc.ch_type == want_type, (
                f"ch{target}: reply describes type {desc.ch_type}, expected {want_type}"
            )

    def test_never_returns_busy(self, wire_transport):
        """MGMT-005: rapid back-to-back requests never yield LSTP_BUSY."""
        for _ in range(64):
            status, _ = wire_transport.request(
                0,
                proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG,
                proto.pack_ch0_read_req(0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX),
                raise_on_error=False,
            )
            assert status != proto.Status.BUSY, "device returned LSTP_BUSY"

    def test_command_latency_bounded(self, wire_transport):
        """MGMT-006: ch0 exchanges meet the latency *policy*, not just the timeout.

        Asserts against the product target (``LSTP_LATENCY_TARGET_MS``) rather
        than only the hard give-up ceiling (``USB_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS``). A few
        exchanges are timed and the *median* is checked, so an isolated USB
        scheduling hiccup does not flake the test, while every single sample is
        still required to stay under the transport timeout.
        """
        wire_transport.drain()
        samples_ms: list[float] = []
        for _ in range(10):
            start = time.monotonic()
            ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
            elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - start) * 1000
            assert elapsed_ms < proto.USB_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS, (
                f"ch0 read took {elapsed_ms:.1f} ms (>= timeout {proto.USB_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS} ms)"
            )
            samples_ms.append(elapsed_ms)
        median_ms = statistics.median(samples_ms)
        assert median_ms < proto.LSTP_LATENCY_TARGET_MS, (
            f"median ch0 latency {median_ms:.2f} ms exceeds the "
            f"{proto.LSTP_LATENCY_TARGET_MS} ms policy target "
            f"(samples={[f'{s:.1f}' for s in samples_ms]})"
        )


class TestNegatives:
    """Malformed / out-of-range requests reject and stay synced."""

    def test_invalid_channel_id(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """MGMT-008: a command to a channel past max is rejected.

        The spec requires a deterministic reject (LSTP_NOT_SUPP). A part that
        instead *silently drops* the request leaves the host to infer the refusal
        from a timeout, which is deviation E4131-11 -- named for the only part
        currently known to do it. The spec-correct assertion is kept, and a
        no-response timeout reports the deviation instead of hard-failing.
        """
        import transport as tr

        bad = wire_discovery.num_channels + 50
        try:
            helpers.expect_reject(wire_transport, bad, 0x00)
        except tr.TransportError:
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding E4131-11: out-of-range channel id is silently dropped "
                "(no reject response); host must rely on timeout"
            )
        _assert_still_synced(wire_transport)

    def test_short_header(self, wire_transport):
        """RAS-007: a sub-header (<4 byte) bulk-OUT is discarded silently, no desync.

        SADD RAS-007 requires an incomplete header to be discarded without a
        response and without desynchronizing the link. Spec-correct: no frame
        comes back for the runt (it is dropped, not answered) and a valid
        exchange still works afterwards. This hub instead answers the runt with an
        error response (finding F14); when it does, the test verifies the reply is
        a *defined error* frame (not a stale/valid reply) and that the link stays
        synced, then xfails citing F14 rather than passing on a silent discard it
        did not perform.
        """
        wire_transport.drain()
        wire_transport.send_raw(b"\x00\x00")
        stray = wire_transport.try_recv_raw(timeout_ms=300)
        if stray is not None:
            hdr = proto.parse_header(stray)
            assert hdr.is_response and hdr.code != proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
                f"sub-header runt drew a non-error reply ({stray.hex()}); a runt "
                "must never be answered as a successful command"
            )
            _assert_still_synced(wire_transport)
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F14: a sub-header (<4 byte) bulk-OUT is answered with an "
                f"error response (0x{stray.hex()}); RAS-007 requires a silent discard"
            )
        _assert_still_synced(wire_transport)

    def test_payload_shorter_than_declared(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """RAS-015/MGMT-009: a header whose declared length exceeds the delivered
        bytes must be deterministically rejected -- never satisfied from a buffer
        still holding the *previous* request's bytes.

        Spec-correct assertion: prime the device with a distinctive named-channel
        read, then send a header-only READ_CONFIG that declares 32 payload bytes
        but carries none. The reply must NOT echo the primed channel's descriptor
        (which would prove the stale buffer was re-parsed and re-executed). On this
        firmware it does echo it (finding F9: declared-vs-delivered length is not
        validated), so the test xfails citing F9; it flips to a hard pass once the
        device validates the length / rejects. The link stays synced either way
        (always drained afterward).
        """
        sub = next(
            (c for c in wire_discovery.channels if c.ch_type != proto.ChannelType.MGMT), None
        )
        target = sub.ch_id if sub else 0
        want_type = sub.ch_type if sub else proto.ChannelType.MGMT

        # Prime the device's request buffer with a distinctive read, capture its
        # reply, then drain (draining is host-side; it does not reset the device
        # buffer -- see finding F9).
        wire_transport.drain()
        wire_transport.send_raw(_ch0_read_frame(target))
        primed = wire_transport.recv_raw()
        assert proto.parse_ch_desc(primed[proto.HEADER_SIZE :]).ch_type == want_type

        # Header-only READ_CONFIG: declares 32 payload bytes, delivers none.
        wire_transport.drain()
        wire_transport.send_raw(proto.pack_header(0, proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG, 32))
        resp = wire_transport.try_recv_raw(timeout_ms=proto.USB_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS)
        try:
            assert resp is not None, "no response to short-payload frame (silent drop)"
            hdr = proto.parse_header(resp)
            stale_reparse = (
                hdr.is_response
                and hdr.code == proto.Status.SUCCESS
                and len(resp) >= proto.HEADER_SIZE + proto.CH_DESC_SIZE
                and proto.parse_ch_desc(resp[proto.HEADER_SIZE :]).ch_type == want_type
            )
            if stale_reparse:
                deviations.xfail(
                    "finding F9: the under-length frame re-parsed the previous "
                    "request's stale buffer instead of being rejected "
                    f"(code=0x{hdr.code:02x}); SADD RAS-015/MGMT-009 require "
                    "deterministic rejection"
                )
            # Spec-correct: the under-length frame is not answered from stale
            # buffer contents (rejected / not re-parsed).
            assert not stale_reparse
        finally:
            wire_transport.drain(timeout_ms=200)
        _assert_still_synced(wire_transport)

    def test_payload_longer_than_declared(self, wire_transport):
        """MGMT-009: extra trailing bytes past the declared length are ignored; the
        declared-length request is honored normally (deterministic, no desync).

        A valid READ_CONFIG with 4 junk bytes appended still returns the normal
        ch0 descriptor (SUCCESS): the device frames on the declared length and
        drops the trailing bytes. The reply body is required to be identical
        across repeats so the trailing bytes provably have no effect.
        """
        req = proto.pack_ch0_read_req(0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        frame = proto.build_request(0, proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG, req) + b"\xde\xad\xbe\xef"
        bodies: list[bytes] = []
        for _ in range(4):
            wire_transport.drain()
            wire_transport.send_raw(frame)
            resp = wire_transport.try_recv_raw(timeout_ms=proto.USB_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS)
            assert resp is not None, "no response to trailing-bytes frame"
            hdr = proto.parse_header(resp)
            assert hdr.is_response and hdr.code == proto.Status.SUCCESS
            desc = proto.parse_ch_desc(resp[proto.HEADER_SIZE :])
            assert desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT
            bodies.append(resp[proto.HEADER_SIZE :])
        assert len(set(bodies)) == 1, "response to trailing-bytes frame not deterministic"
        _assert_still_synced(wire_transport)

    def test_unsupported_command_skips_payload(self, wire_transport):
        """MGMT-007: an unsupported cmd's N-byte payload is skipped, next cmd parsed.

        SADD MGMT-007 requires the device to skip *exactly* the declared payload
        of an unsupported command and then parse the following command correctly.
        To prove the skip (not just "no desync"), a reserved command 0x7E with an
        8-byte payload is packed *immediately before* a valid ch0 READ_CONFIG in a
        single bulk-OUT. If the N-byte skip works, the trailing valid read is
        parsed and answered with a SUCCESS MGMT descriptor.

        On this firmware the trailing frame sharing the USB packet is dropped
        (finding F2: per-USB-packet framing), so the valid reply never appears
        and the test xfails citing F2; it flips to a hard pass once the device
        skips the payload and parses the next command within the packet. The link
        is drained and re-synced afterwards regardless.
        """
        payload = b"\x11" * 8
        packed = proto.build_request(0, 0x7E, payload) + _valid_ch0_read_frame()

        wire_transport.drain()
        wire_transport.send_raw(packed)
        responses: list[bytes] = []
        try:
            r = wire_transport.try_recv_raw(timeout_ms=proto.USB_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS)
            while r is not None:
                responses.append(r)
                r = wire_transport.try_recv_raw(timeout_ms=200)
        finally:
            wire_transport.drain(timeout_ms=200)

        def _is_valid_read_reply(resp: bytes) -> bool:
            if len(resp) < proto.HEADER_SIZE + proto.CH_DESC_SIZE:
                return False
            hdr = proto.parse_header(resp)
            if not (hdr.is_response and hdr.code == proto.Status.SUCCESS):
                return False
            return proto.parse_ch_desc(resp[proto.HEADER_SIZE :]).ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT

        if not any(_is_valid_read_reply(r) for r in responses):
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F2: the command following an unsupported cmd in the same "
                "bulk-OUT was dropped; SADD MGMT-007 requires the N-byte payload "
                "to be skipped and the next command parsed "
                f"(responses={[r.hex() for r in responses]})"
            )
        _assert_still_synced(wire_transport)

class TestBulkPacking:
    """Multiple LSTP packets in one bulk transfer (USB-008)."""

    def test_two_packets_one_bulk_out(self, wire_transport):
        """USB-008: two requests packed in one bulk-OUT get two responses.

        Distinct from per-channel serialization (F-note in the findings doc):
        bulk packing is a USB-transport feature. A firmware that answers only the
        first frame and drops the rest is deviation F2, reported per target via
        the deviation registry rather than a blanket xfail marker, so a part that
        does implement packing is still held to it. The link is drained afterward
        to recover from the unanswered frame.
        """
        import transport as tr

        wire_transport.drain()
        packed = _valid_ch0_read_frame() + _valid_ch0_read_frame()
        wire_transport.send_raw(packed)
        try:
            answered = 0
            for _ in range(2):
                try:
                    hdr = proto.parse_header(wire_transport.recv_raw())
                except tr.TransportError:
                    break
                assert hdr.is_response and hdr.code == proto.Status.SUCCESS
                answered += 1
            if answered < 2:
                deviations.xfail(
                    f"finding F2: only {answered} of 2 frames packed into one "
                    "bulk-OUT were answered; the remainder is dropped instead "
                    "of being processed"
                )
        finally:
            wire_transport.drain(timeout_ms=200)

    def test_large_payload_spanning_packets_reassembled(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """USB-008 (large payload): a single LSTP frame whose payload spans more
        than one USB packet must be reassembled and parsed as one frame, not
        executed per USB packet.

        Spec-correct assertion: a *distinctive* request -- a read of a named
        subsystem channel -- is planted so it begins exactly at the overflow
        packet boundary of one large ``READ_CONFIG`` frame. If the device honors
        USB-008 (reassembles), that planted read is never executed as its own
        command, so its standalone reply must NOT appear among the responses. On
        this firmware the overflow packet IS executed as the planted read
        (finding F2: per-USB-packet framing), so the test xfails citing F2; it
        flips to a hard pass once the device reassembles spanning payloads. All
        reads; no ``WRITE_CONFIG`` (would risk ch0, finding F6). The link is
        always drained afterwards to recover.
        """
        sub = next(
            (c for c in wire_discovery.channels if c.ch_type != proto.ChannelType.MGMT), None
        )
        target = sub.ch_id if sub else 0
        planted = proto.build_request(
            0, proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG, proto.pack_ch0_read_req(target, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        )

        # Standalone response for the planted request: the signature to find.
        wire_transport.drain()
        wire_transport.send_raw(planted)
        baseline = wire_transport.recv_raw()

        # One frame whose declared payload overflows a full USB packet; the
        # planted read is positioned to start exactly at the overflow boundary.
        tx = wire_transport.bulk_tx_size
        filler = b"\x00" * (tx - proto.HEADER_SIZE)
        big = len(filler) + len(planted)
        frame = proto.pack_header(0, proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG, big) + filler + planted
        assert len(frame) > tx

        responses: list[bytes] = []
        wire_transport.drain()
        wire_transport.send_raw(frame)
        try:
            r = wire_transport.try_recv_raw(timeout_ms=proto.USB_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS)
            while r is not None:
                responses.append(r)
                r = wire_transport.try_recv_raw(timeout_ms=250)
        finally:
            wire_transport.drain(timeout_ms=300)

        # The big frame's own reply is a rejection with an empty body; the planted
        # channel descriptor appears only if the overflow packet was executed as
        # our distinct request -> per-USB-packet framing (USB-008 not honored).
        if baseline in responses:
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F2: the overflow packet was executed as the planted "
                "request (per-USB-packet framing); SADD USB-008 requires the "
                "spanning payload to be reassembled and parsed as one frame "
                f"(responses={[r.hex() for r in responses]})"
            )
        # Spec-correct: the spanning payload was consumed as one frame, so the
        # planted request never ran on its own.
        assert baseline not in responses


class TestUsbReset:
    """USB reset recovery and repeated reset cycling (USB-005, STRS-002).

    These re-enumerate the device (seconds each) via the transport's
    ``reset_and_reclaim`` and are marked ``slow`` so the fast suite skips them.
    Each asserts the device comes back with the same channel set and answers a
    valid ch0 exchange -- i.e. a bus-level reset is fully recoverable over the
    wire path.

    @staticmethod
    def _channel_ids(disc) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        return [(c.ch_id, c.ch_type) for c in disc.channels]

    @pytest.mark.slow
    def test_hub_reset_recovery(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """USB-005: the hub re-enumerates and LSTP works after a USB reset."""
        before = self._channel_ids(wire_discovery)
        wire_transport.reset_and_reclaim()
        res = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT
        after = ch0.discover(wire_transport)
        assert self._channel_ids(after) == before, "channel set changed across a USB reset"

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "profile", ["smoke", pytest.param("soak", marks=[pytest.mark.slow, pytest.mark.stress])]
    )
    def test_reset_cycling(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery, profile, soak_cycles):
        """STRS-002: repeated USB reset cycles all recover cleanly.

        Re-enumeration is slow (seconds each). Two profiles: ``smoke`` (default,
        unconditional) runs a small fixed cycle count to prove reset recovery is
        *repeatable*; ``soak`` (marked slow+stress) runs the full SADD 500-cycle
        count (or ``--soak-cycles``), the wire-observable half of STRS-002 (SADD
        explicitly allows programmatic USB resets). Every cycle must re-claim,
        answer a valid ch0 read, and preserve the channel set. The "no stale
        Linux device nodes" clause stays in the driver suite.
        """
        before = self._channel_ids(wire_discovery)
        cycles = (
            (soak_cycles or _STRS002_SOAK_CYCLES) if profile == "soak" else _STRS002_SMOKE_CYCLES
        )
        for i in range(cycles):
            wire_transport.reset_and_reclaim()
            res = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
            assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT, f"cycle {i}: bad ch0 read"
            after = ch0.discover(wire_transport)
            assert self._channel_ids(after) == before, (
                f"cycle {i}: channel set changed across reset"
            )

def _uart_disabled_write_status(transport, ch_id, timeout_ms=1500):
    """Return the Status of an empty UART TX WRITE, tolerant of the live console.

    The ``ehub`` UART is wired to a Linux serial console that emits unsolicited RX
    frames; an *empty* payload avoids a console echo, and any stray RX frame is
    acked and skipped so we read the WRITE's own response. Returns ``None`` if no
    response arrives (which would indicate a link stall).
    """
    softloop.flush_rx(transport, ch_id, quiet_ms=120, max_ms=1200)
    transport.send_raw(proto.build_request(ch_id, uart.UartCmd.WRITE, b""))
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_ms / 1000.0
    status = None
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        frame = transport.try_recv_raw(timeout_ms=100)
        if frame is None:
            continue
        hdr = proto.parse_header(frame)
        if hdr.is_response and hdr.ch_id == ch_id:
            status = hdr.code
            break
        if not hdr.is_response:
            uart.send_rx_ack(transport, ch_id)
    softloop.flush_rx(transport, ch_id, quiet_ms=120, max_ms=600)
    transport.drain()
    return status


class TestReadConfig:
    """ch0 READ_CONFIG status, offsets, and framing (CFG-004/008/009, DISC-009)."""

    def test_read_ch0_succeeds(self, wire_transport):
        """CFG-004: a valid ch0 READ_CONFIG returns a parseable config."""
        res = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT
        cfg = proto.parse_ch0_config(res.config)
        assert cfg.lstp_version == proto.LSTP_VERSION
        assert 1 <= cfg.num_channels < proto.MAX_CHANNELS

    def test_read_invalid_channel_rejected(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """CFG-004: READ_CONFIG for a channel past the max is rejected."""
        bad = wire_discovery.num_channels + 50
        status, _ = ch0.request_read_config(wire_transport, bad, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        assert status != proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
            f"READ_CONFIG for out-of-range channel {bad} unexpectedly succeeded"
        )

    def test_read_invalid_offset_rejected(self, wire_transport):
        """CFG-004/DISC-009: an out-of-range READ_CONFIG offset never corrupts the stream.

        SADD wording is "trim available data rather than corrupting the stream".
        On this hub an offset past the ch0 config is answered deterministically
        with LSTP_ERROR (or an empty SUCCESS body) -- a stricter form of "trim":
        zero bytes returned, never stale/among-frame data. Checked twice for
        determinism, and the link stays synced afterwards.
        """
        clen = len(ch0.read_all_config(wire_transport, 0).config)
        for _ in range(2):
            status, body = ch0.request_read_config(wire_transport, 0, clen + 0x1000, 16)
            if status == proto.Status.SUCCESS and body:
                deviations.xfail(
                    "finding E4131-1: an out-of-range ch0 READ_CONFIG offset is neither "
                    f"trimmed nor rejected -- offset {clen + 0x1000} answered "
                    f"SUCCESS with {len(body)} byte(s), so the offset field is not "
                    "bounds-checked"
                )
            assert (status in (proto.Status.ERROR, proto.Status.TOO_LARGE)) or (
                status == proto.Status.SUCCESS and body == b""
            ), (
                f"out-of-range ch0 read offset not trimmed/rejected: "
                f"status={status!r} len={len(body)}"
            )
        # Still synced.
        res = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT

    def test_stays_synced_after_bad_read(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """CFG-004: a rejected read does not desync the next valid read."""
        bad = wire_discovery.num_channels + 50
        ch0.request_read_config(wire_transport, bad, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        res = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT

    def test_partial_offset_consistency(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """CFG-009: a slice read at a nonzero offset matches the full read.

        Scoped to a channel that honors offset reads -- some channels (MMIO here,
        finding F3) reject offset>0 with LSTP_ERROR, which is a capability
        difference, not a failure of this assertion.
        """
        ch = ch0.first_partial_read_channel(wire_discovery, wire_transport)
        if ch is None:
            pytest.skip("no channel honors nonzero-offset reads (finding F3)")
        full = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX).config
        if len(full) < 2:
            pytest.skip("channel config too small to slice")
        offset, length = 1, min(len(full) - 1, 8)
        sliced = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, offset, length).config
        expected = full[offset : offset + length]

        cap = ch0.max_config_len(wire_transport)
        status, body = ch0.request_read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, cap + 1024)
        if status == proto.Status.SUCCESS:

        else:

    def test_per_channel_read_bounds(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """RAS-002: every enumerated channel enforces READ_CONFIG bounds.

        Runs the bounds sweep over ch0 *and every discovered subsystem channel*
        -- on the 4-channel EVK image that now includes I2C and UART, not just
        MMIO/GPIO -- so the check is not ch0-only. For each channel three
        conditions must hold:

        * an over-large ``length`` is clamped or rejected and never returns more
          than the bulk-IN capacity (no buffer overrun);
        * a far out-of-range offset (``0xFFF0``) and an offset just past the
          channel's real config length are both rejected with an *empty* body --
          never stale bytes (cf. F9) -- and this is deterministic (checked
          twice); and
        * the link is still synced after the whole sweep.

        Confirmed uniform across MGMT/MMIO/GPIO/I2C/UART on ehub: oversized reads
        clamp to the descriptor and OOB offsets return ``LSTP_ERROR`` with no
        body.
        """
        cap = ch0.max_config_len(wire_transport)
        rx = wire_transport.bulk_rx_size
        reject = (proto.Status.ERROR, proto.Status.TOO_LARGE, proto.Status.NOT_SUPP)
        channels = [0] + [c.ch_id for c in wire_discovery.channels]
        for ch_id in channels:
            # Over-large length: clamped or rejected, never overruns the IN buffer.
            status, body = ch0.request_read_config(wire_transport, ch_id, 0, cap + 1024)
            if status == proto.Status.SUCCESS:
                assert len(body) <= rx, (
                    f"ch{ch_id}: oversized read returned {len(body)} B > rx cap {rx}"
                )
            else:
                assert status in reject, f"ch{ch_id}: oversized read status {status!r}"

            # Out-of-range offsets: rejected with no body, and deterministic (no
            # stale-buffer reply). One offset is far past any config; the other
            # is just past this channel's real config length.
            clen = len(ch0.read_all_config(wire_transport, ch_id).config)
            for offset in (0xFFF0, clen + 16):
                for _ in range(2):
                    status, body = ch0.request_read_config(wire_transport, ch_id, offset, 8)
                    if status not in reject:
                        deviations.xfail(
                            f"finding E4131-1: ch{ch_id} accepted out-of-range "
                            f"READ_CONFIG offset {offset} (status {status!r}, "
                            f"{len(body)} byte(s)) instead of rejecting it"
                        )
                    assert status in reject, (
                        f"ch{ch_id}: offset {offset} not rejected (status {status!r})"
                    )
                    assert body == b"", (
                        f"ch{ch_id}: offset {offset} returned {len(body)} stale byte(s)"
                    )

        # The whole bounds sweep left the link synced.
        res = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT

    def test_chunked_read_reassembles(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """DISC-009: reading a channel in slices reassembles the whole config.

        Requires offset-read support, so it targets a partial-read-capable
        channel (finding F3) and skips if none is present.
        """
        target = ch0.first_partial_read_channel(wire_discovery, wire_transport)
        if target is None:
            pytest.skip("no channel honors nonzero-offset reads (finding F3)")
        whole = ch0.read_all_config(wire_transport, target.ch_id).config
        if len(whole) < 4:
            pytest.skip("channel config too small to chunk")
        half = len(whole) // 2
        a = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, target.ch_id, 0, half).config
        b = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, target.ch_id, half, len(whole) - half).config
        if a + b != whole and b[: len(a)] == a:
            deviations.xfail(
                f"finding E4131-1: ch{target.ch_id} slice at offset {half} replayed the "
                "leading bytes instead of continuing, so chunked reads cannot "
                "reassemble a config larger than one response"
            )
