class TestConfigMode:
    """Config-mode / lock-state read+set (CFG-006), the basis for non-destructive
    config-write tests.

    WRITE_CONFIG_MODE (0x0A) / READ_CONFIG_MODE (0x0B) select where WRITE_CONFIG
    lands: NON_VOLATILE (0x00 To-Flash/OTP), FUSED_LOCKED (0x01, irreversible),
    or VOLATILE (0x02 To-RAM, power-cycle reverts). The mutating config tests run
    in VOLATILE so their writes are non-destructive; this class confirms the
    mechanism up front. FUSED_LOCKED is never written here.
    """

    def test_config_mode_readable(self, wire_transport):
        """SVC-001/SVC-005: READ_CONFIG_MODE reports a known, non-fused state.

        A pure read -- it never sends WRITE_CONFIG_MODE. Must decode to a
        documented mode and, on a bring-up rig, must not be fused/locked (which
        would make the part unprovisionable).
        """
        mode = ch0.read_config_mode(wire_transport)
        assert mode is not None, "READ_CONFIG_MODE did not return a decodable mode"
        assert mode != proto.ConfigMode.FUSED_LOCKED, (
            f"device reports {mode.name}: config is fused/locked"
        )

    def test_volatile_mode_round_trips(self, wire_transport):
        """CFG-006: setting the config mode reads back the value that was written.

        Confirms the non-destructive-write mechanism the mutating tests rely on:
        write VOLATILE (0x02) then NON_VOLATILE (0x00) and check each reads back
        the exact value written (proving the response tracks the request, not a
        constant). Both are reversible; FUSED_LOCKED (0x01) is never written. The
        entry mode (the session default, VOLATILE) is restored, so the device is
        left ready for the other tests.
        """
        entry = ch0.read_config_mode(wire_transport)
        assert entry is not None and entry != proto.ConfigMode.FUSED_LOCKED, (
            f"unexpected entry config mode {entry!r}"
        )
        try:
            for mode in (proto.ConfigMode.VOLATILE, proto.ConfigMode.NON_VOLATILE):
                status = ch0.write_config_mode(wire_transport, mode)
                if status == proto.Status.NOT_SUPP:
                    deviations.xfail(
                        f"finding E4131-3: WRITE_CONFIG_MODE({mode.name}) answers "
                        "NOT_SUPP -- the part offers no to-RAM config mode, so every "
                        "config write necessarily targets non-volatile storage"
                    )
                assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
                    f"WRITE_CONFIG_MODE({mode.name}) not accepted"
                )
                assert ch0.read_config_mode(wire_transport) == mode, (
                    f"config mode did not read back {mode.name} after writing it"
                )
        finally:
            # Restore the session default (VOLATILE) so writes stay non-destructive.
            ch0.write_config_mode(wire_transport, entry)
        # Link still synced.
        res = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT


class TestWriteConfig:
    """ch0 WRITE_CONFIG status and rejection (CFG-005/002).

    Every mutating test here uses :func:`ch0.config_restored`, which runs the
    body in VOLATILE (To-RAM) config mode and restores the snapshot afterwards,
    so no write persists to Flash/OTP -- the tests are non-destructive and a
    power cycle is a belt-and-braces reset, not a requirement.
    """

    def test_idempotent_write_succeeds(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery, volatile_writes):
        """CFG-005: writing each channel's own descriptor back is accepted.

        Exercises EVERY channel, not just the first writable one: a writable-config
        channel (GPIO/I2C/UART) accepts the idempotent descriptor write with
        SUCCESS and reads its descriptor back unchanged; a read-only-config channel
        (MMIO, finding F3) rejects it with NOT_SUPP. At least one channel must be
        writable. Config-body writes are covered by the Tier-4 tests below.
        """
        writable = 0
        for ch in wire_discovery.channels:
            before = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
            status, _ = ch0.write_desc(
                wire_transport,
                ch.ch_id,
                0,
                before.desc.ch_type,
                before.desc.ch_flags,
                before.desc.ch_name,
                raise_on_error=False,
            )
            if status == proto.Status.NOT_SUPP:
                continue  # read-only config channel (MMIO, finding F3)
            assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
                f"ch{ch.ch_id} ({ch.type_name}): idempotent descriptor write -> "
                f"{proto.Status(status).name} (expected SUCCESS or NOT_SUPP)"
            )
            after = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
            assert after.desc.ch_type == before.desc.ch_type
            assert after.desc.ch_name == before.desc.ch_name
            writable += 1
        assert writable, "no channel accepted an idempotent descriptor write (F3)"

    def test_reserved_flag_bits_ignored(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """RAS-010: reserved channel-flag bits must be ignored or rejected (all channels).

        Only bit 0 (ENABLE) is defined in the descriptor ``ch_flags``; the rest
        are reserved. SADD RAS-010 requires reserved bits to be ignored (masked
        off) or the write rejected -- never stored verbatim. For EVERY channel
        that accepts a descriptor write this sets reserved bit 1 (keeping ENABLE)
        and reads the flags back; a read-only channel (MMIO, finding F3) that
        rejects the write is compliant (the bit cannot be stored). Descriptor/flag
        writes *do* latch on this hub (unlike a partial config-body write, finding
        F12) -- confirmed by ENABLE toggling a channel's visibility -- and here the
        reserved bit is *stored* (flags 0x01 -> 0x03, finding F17), so the
        spec-correct assertion xfails. Runs in VOLATILE mode and restores each
        channel's original flags, so nothing persists.
        """
        stored: list[str] = []
        checked = 0
        with ch0.volatile_config(wire_transport):
            for ch in wire_discovery.channels:
                before = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
                orig = before.desc.ch_flags
                try:
                    status, _ = ch0.write_desc(
                        wire_transport,
                        ch.ch_id,
                        0,
                        before.desc.ch_type,
                        orig | 0x02,
                        before.desc.ch_name,
                        raise_on_error=False,
                    )
                    if status != proto.Status.SUCCESS:
                        continue  # read-only channel rejects the write (compliant)
                    checked += 1
                    got = ch0.read_config(
                        wire_transport, ch.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX
                    ).desc.ch_flags
                    if got & 0x02:
                        stored.append(f"{ch.type_name} 0x{orig:02x}->0x{got:02x}")
                    else:
                        assert (got & 0x02) == 0, f"ch{ch.ch_id}: flags 0x{got:02x}"
                finally:
                    ch0.write_desc(
                        wire_transport,
                        ch.ch_id,
                        0,
                        before.desc.ch_type,
                        orig,
                        before.desc.ch_name,
                        raise_on_error=False,
                    )
        if stored:
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F17: reserved channel-flag bit stored verbatim on "
                f"channels {', '.join(stored)}; SADD RAS-010 requires reserved "
                "bits be ignored (masked) or the write rejected"
            )
        assert checked, "no channel accepted a flag write to exercise reserved bits"

    def test_write_reads_back_exact(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """CFG-001 (single image): a distinct config write reads back byte-exact (all channels).

        For EVERY channel with a writable, multi-byte config body, programs a
        *distinct* image (one mid-body byte flipped, via a full-body WRITE_CONFIG
        which applies in VOLATILE on GPIO and UART alike) and asserts READ_CONFIG
        returns the exact layout: the addressed byte holds the new value and every
        other byte is unchanged. This proves program->read-back fidelity for the
        running image, not just that a write is accepted. Channels with no writable
        body (MMIO, finding F3) or a single-byte body too small for a mid-byte flip
        (I2C speed) are skipped; at least one channel must be exercised. Runs in
        VOLATILE mode via :func:`ch0.config_restored`, so the write is reverted.
        The full NVPOR channel-type matrix still needs alternate firmware (Tier 8).
        """
        exercised = 0
        for ch in wire_discovery.channels:
            with ch0.config_restored(wire_transport, ch.ch_id) as snap:
                body = bytes(snap.config)
                if len(body) < 2:
                    continue  # read-only (MMIO) or single-byte (I2C speed) body
                off = len(body) // 2  # a nonzero, mid-body offset
                distinct = bytearray(body)
                distinct[off] ^= 0xFF
                distinct = bytes(distinct)
                status, _ = ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, distinct, offset=0)
                if status != proto.Status.SUCCESS:
                    continue  # read-only config channel (finding F3)
                after = ch0.read_all_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id).config
                assert after == distinct, (
                    f"ch{ch.ch_id} ({ch.type_name}): read-back body is not "
                    f"byte-exact after a distinct full-body write (only offset "
                    f"{off} should differ from the original)"
                )
                exercised += 1
        assert exercised, "no writable multi-byte channel to exercise read-back fidelity"

    def test_partial_write_preserves_neighbours(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """CFG-009: a partial (nonzero-offset) WRITE_CONFIG changes only the
        addressed byte and preserves its neighbours -- swept across all channels.

        For EVERY channel with a writable multi-byte body, a single *distinct* byte
        (current value XOR 0xFF) is written at a mid-body offset. The spec-correct
        readback requires exactly that offset to hold the new value (offset honored)
        with every other byte unchanged (neighbours preserved).

        Result on this hub is channel-split (finding F12): the **GPIO** body applies
        the partial write and reads it back exactly, but the **UART** body answers
        LSTP_SUCCESS and *drops* it -- only a full-body UART write latches
        ("ACK-and-drop"). A false success is a defect: SADD requires a partial write
        to either take effect or be rejected NOT_SUPP, never ACKed without effect.
        Neighbour-preservation is asserted as a hard invariant on every channel that
        ACKs the write (the dropped write corrupts nothing); the apply/read-back
        half xfails naming the ACK-and-drop channels. Runs in VOLATILE via
        ``config_restored`` (I2C's 1-byte body and MMIO's read-only body are too
        small / not writable and are skipped).
        """
        ack_dropped: list[str] = []
        applied = 0
        for ch in wire_discovery.channels:
            with ch0.config_restored(wire_transport, ch.ch_id) as snap:
                body = bytes(snap.config)
                if len(body) < 3:
                    continue  # MMIO (read-only) / I2C (1-byte speed) -- no mid offset
                off = len(body) // 2  # a nonzero, mid-body offset
                new = bytes([body[off] ^ 0xFF])
                status, _ = ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, new, offset=off)
                if status != proto.Status.SUCCESS:
                    continue  # body read-only at a nonzero offset on this channel
                got = ch0.read_all_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id).config
                # Hard invariant: a partial write must never corrupt neighbours,
                # whether or not the addressed byte is applied.
                assert got[:off] == body[:off] and got[off + 1 :] == body[off + 1 :], (
                    f"{ch.type_name}: partial write at {off} changed neighbouring bytes"
                )
                if got[off : off + 1] == new:
                    got2 = ch0.read_all_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id).config
                    assert got2 == got, f"{ch.type_name}: nondeterministic partial-write readback"
                    applied += 1
                else:
                    ack_dropped.append(ch.type_name)
        if ack_dropped:
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F12: a partial (nonzero-offset) config-body write is "
                f"answered LSTP_SUCCESS but does not latch on channels "
                f"{', '.join(ack_dropped)} (neighbours preserved); SADD CFG-009 "
                "requires a partial write to take effect or be rejected NOT_SUPP, "
                "not a false success"
            )
        assert applied, "no channel accepted a nonzero-offset config-body write"

        """CFG-005/CFG-008: a body larger than the channel config is rejected (all channels).

        A WRITE_CONFIG whose body exceeds the channel's config region must be
        answered LSTP_TOO_LARGE/LSTP_ERROR, never silently truncated-and-applied.
        For EVERY writable channel an oversized body (kept within one bulk-OUT so
        this exercises config-size validation, not USB packetization) is sent;

    def test_write_size_boundary(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """CFG-008: WRITE_CONFIG honours the config-region size boundary (all channels).

        For EVERY writable multi-byte channel, a body of exactly the region length
        is accepted (the accept side), while a body one byte past the region --
        whether an oversized body at offset 0 or a single byte at the first
        out-of-region offset -- must be rejected (LSTP_ERROR/LSTP_TOO_LARGE),
        never silently accepted. GPIO enforces the boundary exactly; UART accepts
        both a +1 body and an at-end-offset write (finding F12: UART under-
        validates the region size), so the spec-correct reject side xfails naming
        the non-enforcing channels. (The multi-packet framing / re-sync behaviour
        above the bulk limit is tracked separately under RAS-015.) Runs in VOLATILE
        mode via :func:`ch0.config_restored`, so nothing persists.
        """
        reject = (proto.Status.ERROR, proto.Status.TOO_LARGE, proto.Status.NOT_SUPP)
        not_enforced: list[str] = []
        checked = 0
        for ch in wire_discovery.channels:
            with ch0.config_restored(wire_transport, ch.ch_id) as snap:
                n = len(snap.config)
                if n < 2:
                    continue  # read-only (MMIO) or single-byte (I2C speed) body
                # Accept side: an exact-length (idempotent) body is accepted.
                status, _ = ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, snap.config, offset=0)
                if status != proto.Status.SUCCESS:
                    continue  # body not writable in this mode (finding F3)
                checked += 1
                # One byte past the boundary (oversized body at offset 0).
                over, _ = ch0.request_write_body(
                    wire_transport, ch.ch_id, snap.config + b"\x00", offset=0
                )
                ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, snap.config, offset=0)
                # A single byte at the first out-of-region offset.
                off, _ = ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, b"\x00", offset=n)
                if over not in reject or off not in reject:
                    not_enforced.append(
                        f"{ch.type_name} (+1={proto.Status(over).name}, "
                        f"end@{n}={proto.Status(off).name})"
                    )
        if not_enforced:
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F12: config-region size boundary not enforced on channels "
                f"{', '.join(not_enforced)}; SADD CFG-008 requires oversized / "
                "out-of-region writes be rejected"
            )
        assert checked, "no writable multi-byte channel to exercise the size boundary"

    def test_ch0_malformed_write_rejected(self, wire_transport):
        """CFG-005/DISC-005: a malformed/zero ch0 descriptor write must be rejected.

        The management descriptor governs discoverability, so a WRITE_CONFIG to
        ch0 carrying an all-zero descriptor (blank name, num_channels=0) must be
        rejected (spec-correct) rather than silently accepted. On this firmware it
        is accepted and blanks the interface (finding F6), so the test captures
        the good ch0 descriptor first, restores it unconditionally, re-verifies
        discovery, then xfails citing F6; it flips to a hard pass once ch0 writes
        are validated (or ch0 is write-protected).

        Non-destructive: the whole exchange runs in VOLATILE (To-RAM) config mode
        (:func:`ch0.volatile_config`), so even if the hub blanks the management
        descriptor it does so in RAM only -- the in-test restore returns it, and
        a power cycle would clear it regardless. No Flash/OTP write occurs, so
        this no longer needs ``--allow-destructive``.
        """
        with ch0.volatile_config(wire_transport):
            good = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
            status = None
            try:
                status, _ = ch0.write_desc(
                    wire_transport,
                    0,
                    0,
                    0,
                    0,
                    "",
                    config=b"\x00" * len(good.config),
                    raise_on_error=False,
                )
            finally:
                # Always restore the known-good management descriptor + config.
                ch0.write_desc(
                    wire_transport,
                    0,
                    0,
                    good.desc.ch_type,
                    good.desc.ch_flags,
                    good.desc.ch_name,
                    config=good.config,
                    raise_on_error=False,
                )
            restored = ch0.discover(wire_transport)
        assert restored.num_channels >= 1, "ch0 discovery not restored after malformed write"
        if status == proto.Status.SUCCESS:
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F6: ch0 accepted a malformed/zero descriptor write "
                "(blanks the management interface); SADD requires rejection"
            )
        assert status != proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
            f"malformed ch0 write -> {proto.Status(status).name} (expected rejection)"
        )

    def test_oversized_overflow_rejected_not_reparsed(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery):
        """CFG-008/RAS-015: an oversized bulk-OUT must be rejected as one frame and
        must NOT spawn a spurious second response from its overflow packet.

        Spec-correct assertion (SADD RAS-015/CFG-008): a frame whose total spills a
        *valid* request into a second USB packet is handled as a single unit; the
        trailing bytes must not be re-parsed and executed on their own.

        Method: capture the probe request's response when sent alone; then send
        ``[filler frame exactly one USB packet long][same probe request]`` as a
        single bulk-OUT, so the probe starts at the overflow-packet boundary. The
        probe's standalone reply must NOT reappear as a second, unsolicited
        response.

        The probe deliberately reads a *named subsystem channel*, so its reply
        carries that channel's name (e.g. ``MMIO``/``GPIO``) -- content the
        reserved filler or a zero-parsed packet could never produce, so a match
        unambiguously means the overflow packet was executed as our planted
        request.

        On this firmware that second response DOES appear (finding F1:
        per-USB-packet framing), so the test xfails citing F1; it flips to a hard
        pass once the device consumes the whole transfer as one frame. The link is
        always drained afterwards to recover.
        """
        sub = next(
            (c for c in wire_discovery.channels if c.ch_type != proto.ChannelType.MGMT), None
        )
        target = sub.ch_id if sub else 0
        probe = proto.build_request(
            0, proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG, proto.pack_ch0_read_req(target, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        )

        # Baseline: the probe request's response when sent by itself.
        wire_transport.drain()
        wire_transport.send_raw(probe)
        baseline = wire_transport.recv_raw()

        # Frame 1 is a NON-MUTATING reserved-command frame padded to exactly one
        # USB packet, so the appended probe request lands at the start of the
        # overflow packet (where F1 re-parses it). A WRITE_CONFIG filler must NOT
        # be used here: ch0 WRITE_CONFIG is accepted and would overwrite the
        # management descriptor. The reserved command is answered NOT_SUPP (a
        # reply distinct from the probe's), and its intra-packet padding is
        # dropped (finding F2).
        tx = wire_transport.bulk_tx_size
        reserved_cmd = 0x7E
        filler = proto.pack_header(0, reserved_cmd, 0)
        filler += b"\x00" * (tx - len(filler))
        assert len(filler) == tx

        # Send [filler][probe] as one bulk-OUT and collect every response,
        # always draining so a desync never leaks into later tests.
        responses: list[bytes] = []
        wire_transport.drain()
        wire_transport.send_raw(filler + probe)
        try:
            r = wire_transport.try_recv_raw(timeout_ms=proto.USB_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS)
            while r is not None:
                responses.append(r)
                r = wire_transport.try_recv_raw(timeout_ms=200)
        finally:
            wire_transport.drain(timeout_ms=300)

        # The reserved filler never yields the probe's reply, so finding this
        # baseline among the responses means the trailing request was re-parsed
        # from the overflow packet and executed as if sent on its own.
        if baseline in responses:
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F1: the request injected into the overflow packet was "
                "re-parsed and executed as a separate frame; SADD RAS-015/CFG-008 "
                "require the oversized frame to be rejected as one unit "
                f"(responses={[r.hex() for r in responses]})"
            )
        # Spec-correct: the oversized transfer produced no spurious re-executed
        # response from its overflow packet.
        assert baseline not in responses


class TestChannelEnable:
    """Per-channel enable/disable via the descriptor ENABLE flag (DISC-010).

    Both tests are parametrised over every subsystem channel type so each channel
    reports its own status. Clearing bit 0 (``CH_FLAG_ENABLE``) in a channel's
    descriptor really takes the channel down: its ch0 config read then answers
    LSTP_ERROR and its data path stops serving. Every write runs in VOLATILE mode
    with the original flags restored, so the in-test restore (and a power cycle)
    bring the channel back.

    The data path when disabled is a clean rejection on GPIO and UART (both answer
    LSTP_NOT_SUPP), but on I2C the ENABLE flag write itself is destructive: a bare
    disable->re-enable toggle (nothing in between) leaves the channel reporting
    enabled with working config reads, yet the next bus transaction hangs the bulk
    link (finding F18, isolated 2026-07-23; sticky across USB reset, needs a power
    cycle). So *both* I2C cases are xfailed without being executed -- CI can never
    wedge the shared rig. MMIO cannot be disabled at all (its config is read-only,
    finding F3: the flag write is rejected NOT_SUPP).
    """

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("ch_type", _SUBSYS_TYPES, ids=lambda t: t.name)
    def test_disable_takes_channel_down(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery, ch_type):
        """DISC-010: clearing ENABLE disables this channel (config read -> ERROR).

        Captures the descriptor, clears ENABLE in VOLATILE, and asserts the channel
        is no longer usable, then restores it and re-checks it is usable again. The
        disabled-channel config read returning LSTP_ERROR -- rather than a readable
        descriptor with ENABLE=0 -- is itself a deviation (finding F19: a disabled
        channel should stay identifiable by name/type), so the test xfails on it
        while still confirming the disable by effect. MMIO is read-only config
        (finding F3):
        the flag write is rejected NOT_SUPP and the channel stays up -- asserted as
        the documented exception. I2C is xfailed *without executing*: the ENABLE
        toggle itself corrupts the I2C data path (finding F18), and since this test
        would restore ENABLE and pass on config reads alone, it would silently leave
        the bus wedged for every later I2C data test -- so it is not run.
        """
        ch = next((c for c in wire_discovery.channels if c.ch_type == ch_type), None)
        if ch is None:
            pytest.skip(f"no {ch_type.name} channel on this layout")
        if ch_type == proto.ChannelType.I2C:
            deviations.unsafe_to_probe(
                "F18",
                "toggling the I2C ENABLE flag (clear then restore, even in VOLATILE) "
                "kills the I2C data path -- config reads still report the channel "
                "enabled, but the next bus transaction hangs the bulk link (sticky "
                "across USB reset; recovery needs a power cycle). Isolated to the "
                "ENABLE toggle itself, not to I/O while disabled",
            )
        before = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        orig = before.desc.ch_flags
        # Baseline: the ENABLE bit starts set (so the round-trip below is a real
        # 1 -> 0 -> 1 toggle, not a no-op on an already-clear flag).
        assert before.desc.enabled, f"{ch_type.name} ENABLE not set at baseline"
        disabled_read_deviation = False
        with ch0.volatile_config(wire_transport):
            try:
                status, _ = ch0.write_desc(
                    wire_transport,
                    ch.ch_id,
                    0,
                    before.desc.ch_type,
                    orig & ~proto.CH_FLAG_ENABLE,
                    before.desc.ch_name,
                    raise_on_error=False,
                )
                if status == proto.Status.NOT_SUPP:
                    # Read-only config channel (MMIO, F3): cannot be disabled, so
                    # the flag is unchanged -- read it back and confirm still set.
                    still = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
                    assert still.desc.enabled, (
                        f"{ch_type.name} rejected the disable but is not enabled"
                    )
                    return
                assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
                    f"{ch_type.name}: disable -> {proto.Status(status).name}"
                )
                # DISC-010 / finding F19: the disabled channel SHOULD stay
                # descriptor-readable and report ENABLE=0 so the host can still
                # identify it (name/type). This hub instead answers LSTP_ERROR to a
                # config read of a disabled channel, so the clear can only be proven
                # by *effect* (see test_disabled_channel_rejects_io: the data path
                # answers NOT_SUPP). Keep the spec-correct assertion and xfail the
                # deviation so a firmware fix flips this green.
                try:
                    dis = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
                except proto.LstpStatusError as ei:
                    assert ei.status == proto.Status.ERROR, (
                        f"{ch_type.name}: disabled config read -> "
                        f"{proto.Status(ei.status).name}, expected a readable "
                        "ENABLE=0 descriptor (or LSTP_ERROR, finding F19)"
                    )
                    disabled_read_deviation = True
                else:
                    assert not dis.desc.enabled, (
                        f"{ch_type.name}: descriptor still reports ENABLE set after clearing it"
                    )
            finally:
                ch0.write_desc(
                    wire_transport,
                    ch.ch_id,
                    0,
                    before.desc.ch_type,
                    orig,
                    before.desc.ch_name,
                    raise_on_error=False,
                )
        # Re-enable direction *is* confirmed by reading the flag back: ENABLE is
        # set again and the descriptor {type, name} round-trips unchanged.
        after = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        assert after.desc.enabled, f"{ch_type.name} not re-enabled after restore"
        assert after.desc.ch_flags == orig, (
            f"{ch_type.name}: flags not restored ({after.desc.ch_flags:#04x} != {orig:#04x})"
        )
        assert after.desc.ch_type == before.desc.ch_type
        assert after.desc.ch_name == before.desc.ch_name
        if disabled_read_deviation:
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F19: a disabled channel's ch0 config read returns "
                "LSTP_ERROR instead of a readable ENABLE=0 descriptor, so the host "
                "cannot identify a disabled channel by name/type. The disable itself "
                "is confirmed by effect (data path -> NOT_SUPP)."
            )

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("ch_type", _SUBSYS_TYPES, ids=lambda t: t.name)
    def test_disabled_channel_rejects_io(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery, ch_type):
        """DISC-010: a disabled channel rejects data-path I/O (not just its config).

        GPIO (`GET_VALUE`) and UART (`WRITE`) both answer LSTP_NOT_SUPP while
        disabled -- proving the data path is really down, not just the config view.
        MMIO has no disable path (read-only config, F3) so it is skipped. I2C is
        xfailed *without executing*: a data read to a disabled I2C channel gets no
        response and hangs the bulk link (finding F18), which would wedge the rig.
        The channel is restored to ENABLE afterwards.
        """
        ch = next((c for c in wire_discovery.channels if c.ch_type == ch_type), None)
        if ch is None:
            pytest.skip(f"no {ch_type.name} channel on this layout")
        if ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MMIO:
            pytest.skip("MMIO config is read-only (F3); the channel cannot be disabled")
        if ch_type == proto.ChannelType.I2C:
            deviations.unsafe_to_probe(
                "F18",
                "on I2C the ENABLE flag write itself corrupts the data path -- "
                "clearing ENABLE (to reach this disabled-I/O check) already wedges "
                "the bulk link, and even a clean disable->re-enable toggle kills "
                "subsequent bus I/O (sticky across USB reset; needs a power cycle), "
                "unlike the clean LSTP_NOT_SUPP that GPIO/UART return",
            )
        before = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, ch.ch_id, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
        orig = before.desc.ch_flags
        with ch0.volatile_config(wire_transport):
            try:
                ch0.write_desc(
                    wire_transport,
                    ch.ch_id,
                    0,
                    before.desc.ch_type,
                    orig & ~proto.CH_FLAG_ENABLE,
                    before.desc.ch_name,
                    raise_on_error=False,
                )
                if ch_type == proto.ChannelType.GPIO:
                    status, _ = wire_transport.request(
                        ch.ch_id,
                        gpio.GpioCmd.GET_VALUE,
                        (0).to_bytes(2, "little"),
                        raise_on_error=False,
                    )
                else:  # UART
                    status = _uart_disabled_write_status(wire_transport, ch.ch_id)
                got = proto.Status(status).name if status is not None else "NO-RESPONSE"
                assert status == proto.Status.NOT_SUPP, (
                    f"disabled {ch_type.name} data I/O -> {got}, expected NOT_SUPP"
                )
            finally:
                ch0.write_desc(
                    wire_transport,
                    ch.ch_id,
                    0,
                    before.desc.ch_type,
                    orig,
                    before.desc.ch_name,
                    raise_on_error=False,
                )


class TestServiceability:
    """Security/serviceability over the wire (SVC-001/005)."""

    def test_no_production_fw_update(self, wire_transport):
        """SVC-001: production ROM exposes no firmware-update path on ch0.

        The protocol defines four management opcodes -- READ_CONFIG (0x08),
        WRITE_CONFIG (0x09), WRITE_CONFIG_MODE (0x0A) and READ_CONFIG_MODE (0x0B);
        none is a firmware-update or provisioning command. This test:

        * pins that documented set, so a future FW-update/mfg opcode added to the
          protocol layer trips this test rather than sneaking in; and
        * sweeps the *entire reserved request opcode space* (0x00..0x7F, i.e. the
          request half where bit 7 is clear) minus the documented opcodes, and
          asserts each reserved opcode is answered LSTP_NOT_SUPP/LSTP_ERROR (never
          LSTP_SUCCESS) and never desyncs the link.

        Safety: the sweep sends an *empty* payload and explicitly excludes the two
        state-changing documented opcodes -- WRITE_CONFIG (mutates config) and
        WRITE_CONFIG_MODE (can fuse/lock when given 0x01) -- so it cannot mutate
        or lock the device. (0x0B READ_CONFIG_MODE is a read; it only reports the
        lock state and is excluded as documented, not probed as reserved.) This is
        the authoritative reserved-opcode sweep the earlier single-opcode probe
        was gated on.
        """
        documented = {c.value for c in proto.Ch0Cmd}
        assert documented == {
            proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG,
            proto.Ch0Cmd.WRITE_CONFIG,
            proto.Ch0Cmd.WRITE_CONFIG_MODE,
            proto.Ch0Cmd.READ_CONFIG_MODE,
        }, (
            "ch0 command set changed; review whether a firmware-update/provisioning "
            "opcode was added before trusting this SVC-001 sweep"
        )
        honored = []
        for cmd in range(0x00, 0x80):  # request half only (bit 7 == response flag)
            if cmd in documented:
                continue  # documented opcodes (WRITE_CONFIG/WRITE_CONFIG_MODE mutate)
            status, _ = wire_transport.request(0, cmd, b"", raise_on_error=False)
            if status == proto.Status.SUCCESS:
                honored.append(cmd)
            # The link must stay synced after every reserved opcode.
            res = ch0.read_config(wire_transport, 0, 0, proto.READ_CONFIG_MAX)
            if res.desc.ch_type != proto.ChannelType.MGMT:
                deviations.xfail(
                    f"finding E4131-4: reserved ch0 opcode 0x{cmd:02X} desynced the "
                    f"management link -- the next READ_CONFIG came back as "
                    f"ch_type {res.desc.ch_type!r} instead of MGMT"
                )
            assert res.desc.ch_type == proto.ChannelType.MGMT, (
                f"reserved opcode 0x{cmd:02X} desynced the management link"
            )
        # Spec-correct: no undocumented ch0 opcode is honored (a honored reserved
        # opcode would be a possible undocumented FW-update/provisioning path).
        assert not honored, (
            "reserved ch0 opcode(s) honored (possible undocumented FW-update/"
            f"provisioning path): {[hex(c) for c in honored]}"
        )

    def test_manufacturing_trace(self, wire_transport, wire_discovery, board_cfg):
        """SVC-005: revision + version + layout are captured and matched to the image.

        SADD SVC-005 requires the trace fields to be matched to the programmed
        product image. The wire suite matches them to the board YAML that
        describes that flashed image: bcdDevice decodes as a u16 and the protocol
        version is the expected constant, and -- crucially -- the interface name
        equals the YAML ``device_name`` and the enumerated channel set (count +
        ``<intf>_<ch>`` names + types) equals the YAML ``init.*`` layout. A
        golden bcdDevice can be pinned via ``expected_bcd_device`` in the board
        YAML when the reference value is known.
        """
        assert 0 <= wire_transport.bcd_device <= 0xFFFF
        assert wire_discovery.lstp_version == proto.LSTP_VERSION
        assert wire_discovery.num_channels == len(wire_discovery.channels)
        # Every channel reports a decodable type/name triple.
        for ch in wire_discovery.channels:
            assert isinstance(ch.type_name, str) and ch.type_name

        # Match the captured trace to the programmed image described by the YAML.
        expected_name = str(board_cfg.get("device_name") or "")
        if expected_name:
            assert wire_discovery.intf_name.casefold() == expected_name.casefold(), (
                f"trace interface name {wire_discovery.intf_name!r} != programmed "
                f"image device_name {expected_name!r}"
            )
        expected = _expected_name_types(board_cfg)
        if expected:
            intf = wire_discovery.intf_name

            problems = [
                f"{name}: type {proto.ChannelType(got[name]).name if name in got else '<missing>'}"
                f" != expected {t.name if t else '?'}"
                for name, t in expected.items()
                if name not in got or (t is not None and got[name] != t)
            ]
            assert not problems, (
                "manufacturing trace layout != programmed image (board YAML):\n  "
                + "\n  ".join(problems)
            )
        golden_bcd = board_cfg.get("expected_bcd_device")
        if golden_bcd:  # 0 / null / absent => not pinned
            assert wire_transport.bcd_device == int(golden_bcd), (
                f"bcdDevice 0x{wire_transport.bcd_device:04x} != golden 0x{int(golden_bcd):04x}"
            )

def _board_spi(board_cfg):
    """``(channel_name, cs_count, speed_hz)`` from the board YAML, or Nones."""
    devices = ((board_cfg or {}).get("spi") or {}).get("devices") or {}
    for name, spec in devices.items():
        if spec:
            cs_count = spec[0] if len(spec) > 0 else None
            speed_hz = spec[1] if len(spec) > 1 else None
            return str(name), cs_count, speed_hz
    return None, None, None


def _board_flash(board_cfg):
    """``{cs_index: (flash_type, jedec_bytes)}`` declared for the SPI channel."""
    flashes = ((board_cfg or {}).get("spi") or {}).get("spi_flash") or {}
    out = {}
    for per_cs in flashes.values():
        for cs, spec in (per_cs or {}).items():
            if not spec or len(spec) < 2:
                continue
            out[int(cs)] = (str(spec[0]), bytes(spec[1]))
    return out


@pytest.fixture
def spi_flash(board_cfg):
    """Declared SPI flash parts, or skip when the board defines none."""
    flashes = _board_flash(board_cfg)
    if not flashes:

@pytest.mark.transport("libusb")
class TestSpiTransfer:
    """Full-duplex transfer, chip-select selection and CS hold."""

    def test_full_duplex_returns_rx(self, wire_transport, spi_channel, spi_flash):
        """A WRITE_READ clocks TX out and the target's answer in, on every CS.

        Full duplex is the property under test: the same transfer that shifts the
        JEDEC opcode out must shift the identity bytes in. Comparing against the
        board's declared id also proves the bytes come from the addressed part
        rather than an idle bus.
        """
        for cs_index, (flash_type, expect) in sorted(spi_flash.items()):
            cs = spi.SpiCs.CS1 if cs_index else spi.SpiCs.CS0
            status, got = spi.read_jedec_id(wire_transport, spi_channel.ch_id, cs=cs)
            assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
                f"CS{cs_index}: JEDEC read -> {proto.Status(status).name}"
            )
            assert got == expect, (
                f"CS{cs_index} ({flash_type}): JEDEC id {got.hex()} != declared {expect.hex()}"
            )

    def test_each_chip_select_addressable(self, wire_transport, spi_channel, spi_flash):
        """Each declared chip select selects its own part independently."""
        if len(spi_flash) < 2:
            pytest.skip("board declares fewer than two SPI chip selects")
        seen = {}
        for cs_index in sorted(spi_flash):
            cs = spi.SpiCs.CS1 if cs_index else spi.SpiCs.CS0
            status, got = spi.read_jedec_id(wire_transport, spi_channel.ch_id, cs=cs)
            assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
                f"CS{cs_index} not selectable: {proto.Status(status).name}"
            )
            assert got and set(got) != {0xFF}, (
                f"CS{cs_index} returned an idle bus ({got.hex()}), so that chip "
                "select never asserted"
            )
            seen[cs_index] = got
        assert len(seen) == len(spi_flash)

    def test_cs_hold_across_frames(self, wire_transport, spi_channel, spi_flash):
        """CS stays asserted between two LSTP frames when the flags say so.

        Sends the opcode with ASSERT only, then reads with DEASSERT only. The
        target can only answer if CS remained low across the two separate bulk
        transfers, which is what a command-then-response flash access needs.
        """
        expect = next(iter(sorted(spi_flash.items())))[1][1]
        cid = spi_channel.ch_id
        status, _ = spi.request_write(
            wire_transport, cid, bytes([spi.JEDEC_READ_ID]), assert_cs=True, deassert_cs=False
        )
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, f"WRITE with CS held -> {proto.Status(status).name}"
        status, got = spi.request_read(
            wire_transport, cid, spi.JEDEC_ID_LEN, assert_cs=False, deassert_cs=True
        )
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, f"READ with CS held -> {proto.Status(status).name}"
        assert bytes(got) == expect, (
            f"id read with CS held across frames is {bytes(got).hex()}, expected "
            f"{expect.hex()}; CS was not held between the two frames"
        )

    def test_read_without_command_is_idle(self, wire_transport, spi_channel):
        """Clocking in with no preceding command yields an idle (all-ones) bus.

        Guards the inverse of the transfer tests: a READ that asserts and releases
        CS without sending an opcode must not return stale bytes from an earlier
        transfer.
        """
        status, got = spi.request_read(wire_transport, spi_channel.ch_id, 4)
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, f"idle READ -> {proto.Status(status).name}"
        assert set(bytes(got)) <= {0xFF, 0x00}, (
            f"idle READ returned {bytes(got).hex()}, which looks like stale data "
            "rather than an undriven bus"
        )


@pytest.mark.transport("libusb")
class TestSpiNegatives:
    """Malformed and unsupported SPI requests."""

    def test_unknown_opcode_rejected(self, wire_transport, spi_channel):
        """An undefined SPI opcode is answered LSTP_NOT_SUPP, not ignored.

        Every LSTP request must produce a response; silently dropping one forces
        the host to discover the failure by timeout and risks desynchronising the
        pipe against the next reply.
        """
        # 0x07 is outside the defined opcode range (READ..POSTED_WRITE = 1..4).
        cmd = 0x07 | spi.SpiCs.CS0 | spi.SpiCsFlag.ASSERT | spi.SpiCsFlag.DEASSERT
        try:
            status, _ = wire_transport.request(
                spi_channel.ch_id, cmd, b"\x00", raise_on_error=False
            )
        except Exception as e:
            wire_transport.drain()
            deviations.xfail(
                f"finding E4131-9: undefined SPI opcode 0x07 produced no response at "
                f"all ({type(e).__name__}); LSTP requires an LSTP_NOT_SUPP reply"
            )
        assert status in (proto.Status.NOT_SUPP, proto.Status.ERROR), (
            f"undefined SPI opcode 0x07 -> {proto.Status(status).name}, expected NOT_SUPP/ERROR"
        )

    def test_posted_write_answered(self, wire_transport, spi_channel):
        """POSTED_WRITE either performs the write or refuses it -- but answers.

        The opcode is defined in the protocol yet unused by the kernel driver, so
        a device may legitimately not implement it; it must then say so with
        LSTP_NOT_SUPP rather than leave the request unanswered.
        """
        try:
            status, _ = spi.request_posted_write(
                wire_transport, spi_channel.ch_id, bytes([spi.JEDEC_READ_ID])
            )
        except Exception as e:
            wire_transport.drain()
            deviations.xfail(
                f"finding E4131-9: POSTED_WRITE (opcode 0x04) produced no response at "
                f"all ({type(e).__name__}); LSTP requires every request to be "
                "answered, with LSTP_NOT_SUPP when the opcode is not implemented"
            )
        assert status in (proto.Status.SUCCESS, proto.Status.NOT_SUPP, proto.Status.ERROR), (
            f"POSTED_WRITE -> unexpected status {status:#04x}"
        )

# Pages spanned by the multi-page range sweep (I2C-007 "across a page range").
_EEPROM_SWEEP_PAGES = 3
# Settle time for an EEPROM self-timed write cycle.
_EEPROM_WRITE_S = 0.01
# I2C-006 repeated-read cycle counts: SADD specifies 500 per speed. The default
# ('smoke') profile runs a short pass; the 'soak' profile (marked slow) runs the
# full SADD count against every supported speed.
_I2C006_SOAK_CYCLES = 500
_I2C006_SMOKE_CYCLES = 20
_SUITE = "wire_i2c"


def _addr_key(bus_name: str | None, addr: int) -> str:
    """DeviceRunner key for one I2C address on the active bus."""
    label = bus_name or "i2c"
    return f"{label}@0x{addr:02x}"


def _max_read_len(transport) -> int:
    """Largest READ ``rd_len`` whose response body still fits one RX packet."""
    return transport.bulk_rx_size - proto.HEADER_SIZE


def _max_write_data(transport) -> int:
    """Largest WRITE ``data`` (addr byte + payload) fitting one TX packet."""
    return transport.bulk_tx_size - proto.HEADER_SIZE - 1


def _scratch_offset(size: int, page: int) -> int:
    """Last page of the EEPROM -- a byte region safe to write and restore."""
    return max(0, size - page)

    @pytest.mark.usefixtures("i2c_data_path")
    def test_all_declared_targets_present(
        self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets, board_cfg, i2c_bus_key, request
    ):
        """I2C-002: every board-declared address is present; an absent one errors.

        Presence is probed with a zero-length (address-only) write, whose address
        phase ACKs iff a device answers -- device-type-agnostic, so it works for
        EEPROMs, temp sensors, and GPIO expanders alike (a bare *read* would NACK
        on expanders). Asserts every YAML ``i2c.devices`` address ACKs and a
        synthetic absent address fails the address phase, so the full configured
        population is verified rather than a single representative target. An
        absent target *should* answer LSTP_NACK; this hub returns LSTP_TIMEOUT
        for a missing device (finding F13), so both are accepted as "not present"
        -- the NACK-vs-TIMEOUT semantics are pinned separately in I2C-017.
        """
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        runner = DeviceRunner(
            board_cfg,
            _SUITE,
            "declared_targets_present",
            requires=[(_SUITE, "channel_enumerates", lambda _k: i2c_bus_key)],
            request=request,
        )
        for addr in i2c_targets["all"]:

            def _one(a=addr) -> None:
                wire_transport.drain()
                status, _ = i2c.request_write(wire_transport, cid, a, b"")
                assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
                    f"declared target -> {proto.Status(status).name}"
                )

            runner.run(_addr_key(i2c_bus_key, addr), _one)

        # Synthetic absent address: probed after the declared population.
        def _absent() -> None:
            wire_transport.drain()
            status, _ = i2c.request_write(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["absent"], b"")
            assert status in (proto.Status.NACK, proto.Status.TIMEOUT), (
                f"absent 0x{i2c_targets['absent']:02x} -> {proto.Status(status).name} "
                "(expected NACK, or TIMEOUT per finding F13)"
            )

        runner.run(f"{i2c_bus_key}@absent", _absent)
        runner.finish()

    @pytest.mark.slow
    @pytest.mark.usefixtures("i2c_data_path")
    def test_full_bus_scan_matches_declared(
        self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets, board_cfg, i2c_bus_key, request
    ):
        """I2C-002 (nightly): a full 7-bit bus scan matches the declared population.

        Sweeps the whole 7-bit address range (0x08-0x77) with zero-length
        (address-only) writes, whose address phase ACKs iff a device answers --
        device-type-agnostic, so EEPROMs, temp sensors, and GPIO expanders are
        all detected. Every board-declared address must ACK; and when the bus
        sets ``i2c.fail_on_unexpected`` no *undeclared* address may answer, so
        the scan verifies the exact expected bus population rather than merely
        that declared targets are reachable. An absent address should NACK; this
        hub answers LSTP_TIMEOUT for a missing device (finding F13), so any
        non-SUCCESS status counts as "absent". Marked slow (``nightly``): each
        absent address costs a full bus timeout.
        """
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        declared = set(i2c_targets["all"])
        runner = DeviceRunner(
            board_cfg,
            _SUITE,
            "full_bus_scan",
            requires_all=[(_SUITE, "declared_targets_present")],
            request=request,
        )

        ack: set[int] | None = None

        def ensure_scan() -> set[int]:
            nonlocal ack
            if ack is not None:
                return ack
            found: set[int] = set()
            for addr in range(0x08, 0x78):
                wire_transport.drain()
                status, _ = i2c.request_write(wire_transport, cid, addr, b"")
                if status == proto.Status.SUCCESS:
                    found.add(addr)
            ack = found
            return ack

        for addr in sorted(declared):

            def _one(a=addr) -> None:
                assert a in ensure_scan(), "declared I2C target absent from bus scan"

            runner.run(_addr_key(i2c_bus_key, addr), _one)

        def _unexpected() -> None:
            found = ensure_scan()
            unexpected = sorted(found - declared)
            i2c_cfg = (board_cfg or {}).get("i2c") or {}
            strict = any((i2c_cfg.get("fail_on_unexpected") or {}).values())
            if strict:
                assert not unexpected, (
                    "undeclared I2C devices ACKed the bus scan: "
                    f"{[hex(a) for a in unexpected]} (board sets fail_on_unexpected)"
                )

        runner.run(f"{i2c_bus_key}@unexpected", _unexpected)

        def _usable() -> None:
            ensure_scan()
            wire_transport.drain()
            ok, data = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["present"], 1)
            assert ok == proto.Status.SUCCESS and len(data) == 1, (
                "I2C channel not usable after a full bus scan"
            )

        runner.run(f"{i2c_bus_key}@post_scan", _usable)
        runner.finish()

    @pytest.mark.usefixtures("i2c_data_path")
    def test_absent_target_nacks_and_recovers(
        self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets, board_cfg, i2c_bus_key
    ):
        """I2C-017: an unpopulated address fails the transfer, then channel recovers.

        SADD I2C-017 requires an unpopulated address to answer LSTP_NACK (the
        address phase is not ACKed) for both a read and a write, and the channel
        to recover on the next live transfer. This hub instead answers
        LSTP_TIMEOUT for a missing device (finding F13). The functional core --
        the failed transfer is a defined error *and* the bus recovers -- is
        asserted unconditionally; the spec-correct NACK is then xfail-pinned when
        the hub returns TIMEOUT, so this reads as a documented deviation rather
        than a silent pass.
        """
        skip_unless_passed(board_cfg, _SUITE, i2c_bus_key, "channel_enumerates")
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        absent_err = (proto.Status.NACK, proto.Status.TIMEOUT)
        wire_transport.drain()
        rstatus, _ = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["absent"], 1)
        assert rstatus in absent_err, (
            f"absent read -> {proto.Status(rstatus).name} (expected NACK/TIMEOUT)"
        )
        wire_transport.drain()
        wstatus, _ = i2c.request_write(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["absent"], b"\x00")
        assert wstatus in absent_err, (
            f"absent write -> {proto.Status(wstatus).name} (expected NACK/TIMEOUT)"
        )
        skip_unless_passed(
            board_cfg,
            _SUITE,
            _addr_key(i2c_bus_key, i2c_targets["present"]),
            "declared_targets_present",
        )
        wire_transport.drain()
        ok, data = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["present"], 1)
        assert ok == proto.Status.SUCCESS and len(data) == 1, (
            "channel did not recover after the absent-target error"
        )
        if proto.Status.TIMEOUT in (rstatus, wstatus):
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F13: absent I2C target answers LSTP_TIMEOUT; SADD I2C-017 "
                "requires LSTP_NACK on the unacknowledged address phase"
            )


@pytest.mark.usefixtures("i2c_data_path")
class TestI2cIntegrity:
    def _eeprom(self, i2c_targets):
        if i2c_targets["eeprom"] is None:
            pytest.skip("board YAML declares no I2C EEPROM")
        return (i2c_targets["eeprom"], i2c_targets["eeprom_size"], i2c_targets["eeprom_page"])

    def test_eeprom_write_read_integrity(
        self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets, board_cfg, i2c_bus_key
    ):
        """I2C-005: EEPROM page write is read back byte-for-byte.

        Writes incrementing and walking-bit patterns to the last page via the
        random-address WRITE path, reads them back with a combined WRITE_READ,
        and restores the original page in teardown. The write-page granularity
        is taken from the board YAML EEPROM chip type (so it never wraps).
        """
        addr, size, page = self._eeprom(i2c_targets)
        skip_unless_passed(
            board_cfg, _SUITE, _addr_key(i2c_bus_key, addr), "declared_targets_present"
        )
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        off = _scratch_offset(size, page)

        wire_transport.drain()
        _, original = i2c.request_write_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([off]), page)
        assert len(original) == page

        patterns = [
            bytes(range(page)),  # incrementing
            bytes((1 << i) & 0xFF for i in range(page)),  # walking bit
        ]
        try:
            for pattern in patterns:
                wire_transport.drain()
                i2c.write(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([off]) + pattern)
                time.sleep(_EEPROM_WRITE_S)
                wire_transport.drain()
                back = i2c.write_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([off]), page)
                assert back == pattern, (
                    f"EEPROM off=0x{off:02x}: wrote {pattern.hex()} read {back.hex()}"
                )
        finally:
            wire_transport.drain()
            i2c.request_write(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([off]) + original)
            time.sleep(_EEPROM_WRITE_S)

    def test_eeprom_multipage_range_integrity(self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets):
        """I2C-007: write/read integrity across a multi-page EEPROM range.

        Exercises the SADD "across a page range" case the single-page test does
        not: a region spanning several EEPROM pages is programmed page-by-page
        (a single WRITE wraps within a page, so each page is written on its own
        aligned boundary with a distinct byte at every offset), then read back in
        one combined WRITE_READ that crosses the page boundaries and compared
        byte-for-byte. The original contents are captured up front and restored
        page-by-page in teardown.
        """
        addr, size, page = self._eeprom(i2c_targets)
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        pages = max(2, min(_EEPROM_SWEEP_PAGES, size // page))
        region = pages * page
        base = (size - region) - ((size - region) % page)
        if region < 2 * page or base < 0:
            pytest.skip("EEPROM too small for a multi-page range sweep")

        wire_transport.drain()
        _, original = i2c.request_write_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([base]), region)
        assert len(original) == region, f"range read returned {len(original)} B, expected {region}"

        # Distinct byte at every offset (XOR keeps it different from typical
        # existing content) so a cross-page mis-order or wrap is caught.
        pattern = bytes(((base + i) ^ 0xA5) & 0xFF for i in range(region))
        try:
            for p in range(pages):
                poff = base + p * page
                chunk = pattern[p * page : (p + 1) * page]
                wire_transport.drain()
                i2c.write(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([poff]) + chunk)
                time.sleep(_EEPROM_WRITE_S)
            wire_transport.drain()
            back = i2c.write_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([base]), region)
            assert back == pattern, (
                f"multi-page range base=0x{base:02x} ({pages}p): wrote "
                f"{pattern.hex()} read {back.hex()}"
            )
        finally:
            for p in range(pages):
                poff = base + p * page
                chunk = original[p * page : (p + 1) * page]
                wire_transport.drain()
                i2c.request_write(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([poff]) + chunk)
                time.sleep(_EEPROM_WRITE_S)

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("profile", ["smoke", pytest.param("soak", marks=pytest.mark.slow)])
    def test_read_repeatable(self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets, profile):
        """I2C-006: repeated reads at every supported speed are identical + timed.

        SADD I2C-006 requires many cycles at each supported speed, with data
        correctness and latency statistics. This programs every I2C speed the
        channel supports (0..3 = 100k/400k/1M/3.4M) via ch0 WRITE_CONFIG, then
        reads a stable region (EEPROM memory, else a live register) a fixed
        number of cycles per speed, asserting every read equals the first and
        recording per-speed latency percentiles. The original speed is restored.

        Two profiles: ``smoke`` (default) runs a short cycle count at the current
        speed only; ``soak`` (marked slow) runs the full SADD 500 cycles at every
        supported speed. Note (finding F12): this hub does not validate/apply
        config writes, so a programmed speed may not change the bus timing --
        the per-speed latencies are captured for the bring-up log regardless.
        """
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        use_eeprom = i2c_targets["eeprom"] is not None
        addr = i2c_targets["eeprom"] if use_eeprom else i2c_targets["present"]
        rd_len = 16 if use_eeprom else 2

        def _read() -> bytes:
            wire_transport.drain()
            if use_eeprom:
                return i2c.write_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, b"\x00", rd_len)
            return i2c.read(wire_transport, cid, addr, rd_len)

        def _cycle(cycles: int, label: str) -> None:
            first = _read()
            lat: list[float] = []
            for _ in range(cycles - 1):
                start = time.monotonic()
                got = _read()
                lat.append((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
                assert got == first, f"{label}: read not stable ({got.hex()} != {first.hex()})"
            if lat:
                lat.sort()
                idx = min(len(lat) - 1, max(0, round(0.99 * len(lat)) - 1))
                print(
                    f"I2C-006 {label}: n={cycles} mean={statistics.fmean(lat):.2f} "
                    f"p50={lat[len(lat) // 2]:.2f} p99={lat[idx]:.2f} ms"
                )

        if profile == "smoke":
            _cycle(_I2C006_SMOKE_CYCLES, "current-speed")
            return

        # Soak: sweep every supported speed with the full SADD cycle count.
        with ch0.config_restored(wire_transport, cid) as snap:
            if not snap.config:
                pytest.skip("I2C channel exposes no writable config body")
            for speed in i2c.I2cSpeed:
                body = bytes([int(speed)]) + bytes(snap.config[1:])
                status, _ = ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, cid, body)
                if status != proto.Status.SUCCESS:
                    continue  # unsupported speed on this channel; skip it
                _cycle(_I2C006_SOAK_CYCLES, f"speed={speed.name}")

    def test_combined_write_read(self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets):
        """I2C-010: WRITE_READ (repeated-START) returns the addressed data.

        For an EEPROM, a byte written at a scratch offset is read back through
        the combined path (proving the write phase set the address pointer and
        the read phase returned that exact location). The scratch byte is
        restored afterwards.
        """
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        if i2c_targets["eeprom"] is None:
            # No memory to plant a known value: fall back to proving the
            # combined path is well-formed and deterministic against a live reg.
            addr = i2c_targets["present"]
            wire_transport.drain()
            a = i2c.write_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, b"\x00", 2)
            wire_transport.drain()
            b = i2c.write_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, b"\x00", 2)
            assert len(a) == 2 and a == b
            return

        addr, size, page = self._eeprom(i2c_targets)
        off = _scratch_offset(size, page)
        wire_transport.drain()
        _, original = i2c.request_write_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([off]), 1)
        sentinel = bytes([original[0] ^ 0x5A])
        try:
            wire_transport.drain()
            i2c.write(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([off]) + sentinel)
            time.sleep(_EEPROM_WRITE_S)
            wire_transport.drain()
            got = i2c.write_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([off]), 1)
            assert got == sentinel, (
                f"combined WRITE_READ off=0x{off:02x}: wrote {sentinel.hex()} read {got.hex()}"
            )
        finally:
            wire_transport.drain()
            i2c.request_write(wire_transport, cid, addr, bytes([off]) + original)
            time.sleep(_EEPROM_WRITE_S)


@pytest.mark.usefixtures("i2c_data_path")
class TestI2cBounds:
    def test_read_length_bounds(self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets):
        """I2C-011 / RAS-002: oversized reads -> TOO_LARGE, no desync."""
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        addr = i2c_targets["present"]
        max_rd = _max_read_len(wire_transport)

        wire_transport.drain()
        status, data = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, max_rd)
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS and len(data) == max_rd, (
            f"max read {max_rd} -> {proto.Status(status).name}, got {len(data)}"
        )
        for bad in (max_rd + 1, 0xFFFF):
            wire_transport.drain()
            status, data = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, bad)
            assert status == proto.Status.TOO_LARGE and not data, (
                f"read rd_len={bad} -> {proto.Status(status).name}, "
                f"got {len(data)} bytes (expected TOO_LARGE + empty)"
            )
        # Zero-length read is a valid no-op.
        wire_transport.drain()
        status, data = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, 0)
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS and not data
        # No desync: a normal read still works.
        wire_transport.drain()
        status, data = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, 1)
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS and len(data) == 1

    def test_write_length_bounds(self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets):
        """I2C-011 / RAS-002: an oversized write -> TOO_LARGE before any bus IO.

        The oversized frame is aimed at an *absent* address so that, even if a
        future firmware length-checked it late, it could only NACK -- it can
        never mutate a live target. A normal transfer afterwards proves the
        channel did not desynchronize.
        """
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        over = _max_write_data(wire_transport) + 2
        wire_transport.drain()
        status, _ = i2c.request_write(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["absent"], b"\x00" * over)
        assert status == proto.Status.TOO_LARGE, (
            f"oversized write ({over} B) -> {proto.Status(status).name}"
        )
        # Zero-length write (address-only quick command) is accepted.
        wire_transport.drain()
        status, _ = i2c.request_write(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["present"], b"")
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS
        # No desync.
        wire_transport.drain()
        status, data = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["present"], 1)
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS and len(data) == 1


@pytest.mark.usefixtures("i2c_data_path")
class TestI2cCapabilities:
    def test_bus_recovery_keeps_channel_usable(self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets):
        """I2C-009 (partial): BUS_RECOVERY succeeds and leaves the channel usable.

        A recovery request should be idempotent: on a healthy/idle bus there is
        nothing to clear, so the hub should still answer LSTP_SUCCESS (clock out
        the recovery pulses + STOP) and a subsequent transfer to a live target
        must succeed. On this hub an idle-bus recovery instead answers LSTP_ERROR
        (finding F16) -- a status the driver's ``recover_bus()`` surfaces as a
        failure -- so the spec-correct assertion xfails and I2C-009 is tracked as
        FAIL until firmware clarifies/fixes it. The channel is confirmed usable
        either way (recovery is non-destructive). SADD does not define the
        idle-bus return explicitly; exercising real recovery clocks after a
        stuck-SDA fault needs a bench stimulus (the remainder of I2C-009).
        """
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        wire_transport.drain()
        status, _ = i2c.request_bus_recovery(wire_transport, cid)
        # Hard invariant regardless of the recovery status byte: the channel must
        # still transfer to a live target afterwards.
        wire_transport.drain()
        ok, data = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["present"], 1)
        assert ok == proto.Status.SUCCESS and len(data) == 1, (
            "channel not usable after bus recovery"
        )
        if status == proto.Status.ERROR:
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F16: I2C BUS_RECOVERY on an idle bus answers LSTP_ERROR "
                "instead of LSTP_SUCCESS; the driver's recover_bus() surfaces this "
                "as a failure. SADD leaves the idle-bus return undefined -- tracked "
                "as FAIL until firmware clarifies or fixes it."
            )
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
            f"bus recovery -> {proto.Status(status).name} (expected SUCCESS)"
        )


@pytest.mark.usefixtures("i2c_data_path")
class TestI2cSmbus:
    """SMBus block-command family: block read (I2C-014), PEC (I2C-008) and
    malformed-block handling (RAS-017).

    Real SMBus compliance -- a leading count byte, the 32-byte block cap, PEC
    transport/validation, and rejection of an over-length / short block -- can
    only be verified against a *true SMBus-block-compliant* target. A plain
    EEPROM is not one: it returns raw memory (no count byte) and cannot be told
    to emit a malformed block. Every test here is gated on the ``smbus_target``
    fixture and is reported BLOCKED (skipped) until a compliant device is
    declared under the board YAML ``i2c.smbus`` section. When present, these run
    against the real device and pass/fail on genuine SMBus semantics.
    """

    def _assert_usable(self, wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets):
        wire_transport.drain()
        ok, data = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["present"], 1)
        assert ok == proto.Status.SUCCESS and len(data) == 1, (
            "I2C channel not usable after SMBus transaction"
        )

    def test_smbus_block_read_compliant(
        self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets, smbus_target
    ):
        """I2C-014: SMBUS_BLOCK_READ returns a spec-compliant block.

        SADD I2C-014 requires the hub to implement the SMBus block-read opcode.
        Against a true SMBus block device a conformant reply must:
          * be accepted with LSTP_SUCCESS,
          * lead with a count byte N in 1..32 (SMBus 6.5.7), and
          * carry exactly N payload bytes.
        The channel must remain usable afterwards. (Merely accepting the opcode
        against an EEPROM is not sufficient -- that returns raw memory with no
        count byte -- hence the true-device gate.)
        """
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        addr = smbus_target["addr"]
        cmd = bytes([smbus_target["command"]])
        wire_transport.drain()
        status, body = i2c.request_smbus_block_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, cmd)
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
            f"SMBUS_BLOCK_READ -> {proto.Status(status).name} (expected SUCCESS)"
        )
        assert len(body) >= 1, "SMBus block read returned no leading count byte"
        count = body[0]
        assert 1 <= count <= i2c.SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX, (
            f"SMBus block count {count} outside 1..{i2c.SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX}"
        )
        assert len(body) - 1 >= count, (
            f"block claims {count} bytes but only {len(body) - 1} were delivered"
        )
        self._assert_usable(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets)

    def test_smbus_block_read_pec(self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets, smbus_target):
        """I2C-008: a PEC-enabled block read transports and validates the PEC byte.

        SADD I2C-008 requires the PEC byte to be transported end-to-end so the
        client stack can verify it. With the PEC flag set the reply carries an
        extra trailing byte -- ``[count, data..., PEC]`` -- and the PEC must
        equal CRC-8 over the full transaction. A driver-level emulated PEC test
        already passes (lstp_test.py::TestI2c::test_emulated_smbus_block_read);
        this is the on-wire counterpart against real silicon.
        """
        if not smbus_target["pec"]:
            pytest.skip("declared SMBus target does not support PEC (I2C-008)")
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        addr = smbus_target["addr"]
        cmd = bytes([smbus_target["command"]])
        wire_transport.drain()
        status, body = i2c.request_smbus_block_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, cmd, pec=True)
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
            f"PEC block read -> {proto.Status(status).name} (expected SUCCESS)"
        )
        assert len(body) >= 2, "PEC block read too short to hold count + PEC"
        count = body[0]
        assert len(body) == 1 + count + 1, f"PEC read: expected 1+{count}+1 bytes, got {len(body)}"
        expected = i2c.smbus_block_read_pec(addr, smbus_target["command"], body[:-1])
        assert body[-1] == expected, f"PEC byte 0x{body[-1]:02x} != expected 0x{expected:02x}"
        self._assert_usable(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets)

    def test_smbus_malformed_block_rejected(
        self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets, smbus_target
    ):
        """RAS-017: an over-length / short SMBus block is reported as an error.

        SADD RAS-017: when a target returns a block length greater than 32 (or a
        packet shorter than declared), the host must surface a protocol error and
        subsequent I2C transfers must still succeed. Provoking this needs a
        target (or bus fault injector) that can emit a malformed block, declared
        as ``i2c.smbus.<bus>.malformed`` -- a bench harness. Without it the test
        skips (BLOCKED). When available, the hub must NOT answer LSTP_SUCCESS and
        the channel must recover.
        """
        if not smbus_target["malformed"]:
            pytest.skip(
                "no SMBus malformed-block injector declared (i2c.smbus.malformed)"
                " -- RAS-017 needs a bench fault source"
            )
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        addr = smbus_target["addr"]
        cmd = bytes([smbus_target["command"]])
        wire_transport.drain()
        status, body = i2c.request_smbus_block_read(wire_transport, cid, addr, cmd)
        # With the malformed-block injector active, the transaction MUST surface a
        # protocol error. Any LSTP_SUCCESS is a RAS-017 failure -- either the
        # injector was ignored (a well-formed block came back) or the hub passed a
        # malformed block through as valid. Both mean the fault was not caught.
        assert status != proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
            f"malformed-block read returned LSTP_SUCCESS ({len(body)} B); RAS-017 "
            "requires a protocol error (injector ignored, or a malformed block "
            "accepted as valid)"
        )
        assert status in (proto.Status.ERROR, proto.Status.TOO_LARGE, proto.Status.NACK), (
            f"malformed block -> {proto.Status(status).name} (expected error)"
        )
        # Bus must recover regardless.
        self._assert_usable(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets)


class TestI2cConfig:
    """I2C ch0 config format + write validation (CFG-004 / I2C-003)."""

    def test_config_length_is_sadd_prefix(self, wire_transport, i2c_channel):
        """CFG-004: the I2C config length must be a valid SADD 4.4.1 field prefix.

        SADD 4.4.1 defines the I2C channel config as up to 11 bytes in a fixed
        field order: Speed (1B), Output Drive Strength (2B), Slew Rate (2B),
        Input Debounce (2B), Glitch Filter Width (2B), Bus Low Timeout (1B) and
        Bus Arbitration Retries (1B). A firmware may implement a *prefix* of
        these fields for backward compatibility -- newer optional fields are
        appended at the end -- so any of the cumulative lengths {1,3,5,7,9,10,11}
        is compliant. What is NOT allowed is a length that splits a field in half
        (e.g. 2 or 4 bytes), which would make the exposed config unparseable.

        This hub exposes 1 byte (Speed only), which is the shortest valid prefix
        and therefore PASSES. The drive-strength/slew/debounce/glitch/timeout/
        retry knobs are simply not implemented, which the backward-compatibility
        contract permits.
        """
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        clen = len(ch0.read_all_config(wire_transport, cid).config)
        assert clen in i2c.I2C_SADD_PREFIX_LENGTHS, (
            f"I2C config is {clen} B, which splits a SADD 4.4.1 field; valid "
            f"backward-compatible prefixes are {i2c.I2C_SADD_PREFIX_LENGTHS} "
            f"(full format = {i2c.I2C_SADD_CONFIG_SIZE} B)"
        )

    @pytest.mark.usefixtures("i2c_data_path")
    def test_invalid_speed_rejected(self, wire_transport, i2c_channel, i2c_targets):
        """I2C-003: an unsupported I2C speed must be rejected by WRITE_CONFIG.

        SADD 4.4.1 defines an up-to-11-byte I2C config, but this hub implements
        only the leading ``u8 speed`` (0..3 = 100k/400k/1M/3.4M) -- a valid
        backward-compatible prefix (see ``test_config_length_is_sadd_prefix``),
        so Speed is the only field to validate. Writing an out-of-range speed
        (0x05) must fail with
        LSTP_NOT_SUPP/LSTP_ERROR per the PRD. On this hub the write is accepted
        with LSTP_SUCCESS (finding F12: config writes are not validated), so the
        spec-correct assertion xfails. The config is snapshotted and restored, and
        the channel is confirmed usable afterwards -- writing config performs no
        bus transaction, so this does not disturb attached targets.
        """
        cid = i2c_channel.ch_id
        with ch0.config_restored(wire_transport, cid) as snap:
            if not snap.config:
                pytest.skip("I2C channel exposes no writable config body")
            bad = bytes([0x05]) + bytes(snap.config[1:])
            status, _ = ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, cid, bad)
            if status == proto.Status.SUCCESS:
                deviations.xfail(
                    "finding F12: invalid I2C speed 0x05 accepted with "
                    "LSTP_SUCCESS; SADD I2C-003 requires NOT_SUPP/ERROR"
                )
            assert status in (proto.Status.NOT_SUPP, proto.Status.ERROR), (
                f"invalid I2C speed -> {proto.Status(status).name}"
            )
        # Restore put the good speed back; the channel must still transfer.
        wire_transport.drain()
        ok, data = i2c.request_read(wire_transport, cid, i2c_targets["present"], 1)
        assert ok == proto.Status.SUCCESS and len(data) == 1, (
            "I2C channel not usable after speed-write probe"
        )
