class TestUartRxPath:
    def test_rx_burst_exceeds_tx(self, wire_transport, uart_loopback):
        """UART-002 (RX path): a single 1-byte stimulus yields a larger RX burst.

        Buffers N printable chars on the console line, then sends *one* Ctrl-U
        byte; the canonical kill-line echoes a BS/SP/BS erase run (~3 bytes per
        buffered char). That RX burst is many times the size of the one byte that
        triggered it, so it exercises the RX unsolicited-frame + ack path with a
        volume decoupled from (and larger than) what we transmitted -- safely and
        without an autonomous console source. Larger sustained, non-TX-gated RX
        (UART-011 overrun) needs a bench traffic generator (see coverage doc).
        """
        if uart_loopback.binary_safe:
            pytest.skip(
                "Ctrl-U erase-burst RX test is console line-discipline specific; "
                "N/A on a raw hardware short (--uart-loopback-raw)"
            )
        cid = uart_loopback.ch_id
        n = 64
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)
        # Fill the canonical buffer; drain the echo of the typed chars.
        typed = softloop.printable(n)
        status, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, typed)
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS
        echoed = softloop.flush_rx(wire_transport, cid)
        assert len(echoed) >= n, f"typed echo {len(echoed)} < {n}"

        # One Ctrl-U byte -> a multi-byte erase burst for the buffered line.
        status, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, bytes([softloop.VKILL]))
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS
        burst = softloop.flush_rx(wire_transport, cid, quiet_ms=300, max_ms=3000)
        # The erase run is strictly larger than the single stimulus byte, and is
        # composed only of backspace/space (no CR/LF injected by us).
        assert len(burst) > 1, f"Ctrl-U produced no RX burst ({len(burst)} B)"
        assert set(burst) <= {0x08, 0x20}, (
            f"unexpected bytes in erase burst: {bytes(sorted(set(burst)))!r}"
        )


class TestUartBounds:
    def test_write_length_bounds(self, wire_transport, uart_channel):
        """UART-006 / RAS-002: max TX ok, zero ok, max+1 -> TOO_LARGE, recovers.

        Asserts on TX status only, so it does not depend on the far-end peer. All
        payloads are printable/space and never contain CR/LF, so even against the
        live console nothing is ever submitted to the login. A max+1 frame is 513
        bytes, so the host splits it across two USB packets and the trailing runt
        is re-parsed by the device (finding F1); the runt's stray frame is drained
        before recovery is checked.
        """
        cid = uart_channel.ch_id
        max_tx = wire_transport.bulk_tx_size - proto.HEADER_SIZE

        # Max legal single-frame write succeeds; drain its echo.
        softloop.flush_rx(wire_transport, cid)
        status, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, softloop.printable(max_tx))
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, f"max TX {max_tx} -> {proto.Status(status).name}"
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)

        # Zero-length write is a valid no-op in a clean state.
        status, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, b"")
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS

        # One byte over the packet limit is rejected as TOO_LARGE (spaces only).
        status, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, b"\x20" * (max_tx + 1))
        assert status == proto.Status.TOO_LARGE, (
            f"TX {max_tx + 1} -> {proto.Status(status).name} (expected TOO_LARGE)"
        )
        # The oversized frame's trailing USB-packet runt leaves a stray frame
        # (finding F1); clear it, then prove the channel recovered.
        wire_transport.drain(timeout_ms=100)
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)
        status, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, softloop.printable(8))
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
            f"post-TOO_LARGE recovery TX -> {proto.Status(status).name}"
        )
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)


class TestUartBreak:
    def test_gen_break_supported(self, wire_transport, uart_channel):
        """UART-010: GEN_BREAK is expected to be SUPPORTED.

        SADD UART-010 requires host->device break generation with deterministic
        reporting. A target that does not implement GEN_BREAK returns NOT_SUPP
        (finding F11). The
        spec-correct assertion (SUCCESS) is kept, so this flips to a hard pass
        once GEN_BREAK lands; today's firmware xfails citing F11 after confirming
        the channel is still usable.
        """
        cid = uart_channel.ch_id
        softloop.flush_rx(wire_transport, cid)
        status, _ = uart.gen_break(wire_transport, cid)
        if status == proto.Status.NOT_SUPP:
            usable, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, softloop.printable(8))
            assert usable == proto.Status.SUCCESS, "channel unusable after NOT_SUPP"
            softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)
            deviations.xfail(
                "finding F11: GEN_BREAK returns NOT_SUPP; SADD UART-010 requires "
                "break generation (hub limitation to be fixed)"
            )
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS, (
            f"GEN_BREAK -> {proto.Status(status).name} (expected SUCCESS)"
        )
        # Channel remains usable for ordinary TX (printable, no submit).
        status, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, softloop.printable(8))
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)


class TestUartConfig:
    """UART ch0 config-write validation (UART-004/007).

    The UART channel is wired to a live serial console, so both tests snapshot
    the whole config body and restore it via :func:`ch0.config_restored` before
    returning -- if the hub applies an invalid config (finding F12) the original
    framing is put straight back and the channel is re-checked for usability.
    The UART config body is ``__le32 speed; u8 data_bits; u8 stop_bits;
    u8 parity_flow`` (byte 4 = data_bits, byte 5 = stop_bits).
    """

    def test_invalid_data_bits_rejected(self, wire_transport, uart_channel):
        """UART-004: 5-bit data mode must be rejected, prior settings preserved.

        SADD UART-004 requires WRITE_CONFIG to reject unsupported data-bit widths
        (5/6) with a deterministic error and to leave the previous UART settings
        active. The invalid value is written as a *full-body* config write (a
        partial/offset write is ACKed but does not latch on UART, finding F12), so
        this genuinely exercises value validation: if the hub accepts the 5-bit
        value -- with SUCCESS and the field mutating to 5 -- it did not validate
        (finding F12) and the spec-correct assertion xfails.
        """
        cid = uart_channel.ch_id
        softloop.flush_rx(wire_transport, cid)
        with ch0.config_restored(wire_transport, cid) as snap:
            if len(snap.config) < uart.CONFIG_SIZE:
                pytest.skip("UART channel exposes no writable config body")
            orig = bytes(snap.config)
            # Full-body write with data_bits (offset 4) = 5 (unsupported).
            bad = bytearray(orig)
            bad[4] = 5
            status, _ = ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, cid, bytes(bad), offset=0)
            after = ch0.read_all_config(wire_transport, cid).config
            if status == proto.Status.SUCCESS or after != orig:
                deviations.xfail(
                    "finding F12: 5-bit UART data mode accepted / config mutated "
                    f"(status={proto.Status(status).name}, data_bits->{after[4]}); "
                    "SADD UART-004 requires rejection with prior settings preserved"
                )
            assert status in (proto.Status.NOT_SUPP, proto.Status.ERROR)
            assert after == orig, "UART settings mutated by a rejected write"
        # Channel still transmits after restore (printable, never submitted).
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)
        status, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, softloop.printable(8))
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)

    def test_supported_baud_rates_program(self, wire_transport, uart_channel):
        """UART-003: every SADD-supported baud rate programs and reads back.

        The UART line rate is the ``Speed`` field (``__le32`` at offset 0) of the
        channel config (SADD 4.5.1). Sweeps the supported ladder, writing each
        rate into the config via a *full-body* WRITE_CONFIG and reading it back to
        confirm it took effect at the config layer (electrical line-timing at the
        pin is a bench/driver-termios concern). Runs under
        :func:`ch0.config_restored`, which puts the device in VOLATILE (To-RAM)
        mode -- so the writes apply but a power cycle reverts them, and the
        original rate is restored on exit.

        NB: a *full-body* write is required. A partial/offset write of only the
        4-byte speed field is answered LSTP_SUCCESS but does not latch on this hub
        (finding F12); the restore path and this sweep both write the whole body.
        Value validation is absent (an out-of-ladder rate is also accepted) -- see
        ``TestUartConfig`` -- but every supported rate programs cleanly.
        """
        cid = uart_channel.ch_id
        softloop.flush_rx(wire_transport, cid)
        with ch0.config_restored(wire_transport, cid) as snap:
            body = bytes(snap.config)
            if len(body) < uart.CONFIG_SIZE:
                pytest.skip("UART channel exposes no writable config body")
            failed: list[tuple[int, str, int]] = []
            for baud in _SADD_BAUDS:
                patched = struct.pack("<I", baud) + body[4:]
                status, _ = ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, cid, patched, offset=0)
                got = uart.read_config(wire_transport, cid).speed
                if status != proto.Status.SUCCESS or got != baud:
                    failed.append((baud, proto.Status(status).name, got))
            assert not failed, f"supported baud rates did not program/read back: {failed}"
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)

    def test_invalid_config_no_mutation(self, wire_transport, uart_channel):
        """UART-007: an invalid stop-bits value is rejected with no persistent mutation.

        SADD UART-007 requires invalid config values to fail with LSTP_ERROR and
        leave no persistent config change. This programs an out-of-range
        ``stop_bits`` (5; valid are 1/2) via a *full-body* config write (a
        partial/offset write is ACKed but does not latch on UART, finding F12) and
        asserts rejection + unchanged read-back. If the hub accepts/mutates it did
        not validate (finding F12) and the spec-correct assertion xfails.
        """
        cid = uart_channel.ch_id
        softloop.flush_rx(wire_transport, cid)
        with ch0.config_restored(wire_transport, cid) as snap:
            if len(snap.config) < uart.CONFIG_SIZE:
                pytest.skip("UART channel exposes no writable config body")
            orig = bytes(snap.config)
            # Full-body write with stop_bits (offset 5) = 5 (invalid).
            bad = bytearray(orig)
            bad[5] = 5
            status, _ = ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, cid, bytes(bad), offset=0)
            after = ch0.read_all_config(wire_transport, cid).config
            if status == proto.Status.SUCCESS or after != orig:
                deviations.xfail(
                    "finding F12: invalid UART stop_bits accepted / config mutated "
                    f"(status={proto.Status(status).name}, stop_bits->{after[5]}); "
                    "SADD UART-007 requires LSTP_ERROR and no persistent mutation"
                )
            assert status in (proto.Status.NOT_SUPP, proto.Status.ERROR)
            assert after == orig
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "mode",
        [uart.Flow.XONXOFF, uart.Flow.RTSCTS, uart.Flow.DTRDSR],
        ids=["xonxoff", "rtscts", "dtrdsr"],
    )
    def test_flow_control_policy(self, wire_transport, uart_channel, mode):
        """UART-005: unsupported flow-control modes must be rejected or ignored.

        SADD UART-005 keeps the UART in no-flow operation and requires any attempt
        to select XON/XOFF, RTS/CTS or DSR/DTR to be either *rejected*
        (LSTP_ERROR/NOT_SUPP, prior settings preserved) or *ignored* (accepted but
        the effective flow mode stays NONE) -- the hub has no hardware flow lines,
        so it must not advertise a mode it cannot perform. Flow is the high nibble
        of the ``parity_flow`` byte (offset 6) of the ch0 UART config; this writes
        it as a *full-body* config write (a partial/offset write is ACKed but does
        not latch on UART, finding F12) and inspects the status + read-back.

        The electrical handshake itself (does RTS/CTS or XON/XOFF actually gate the
        byte stream) needs modem-control lines and an analyzer/peer -- this rig's
        UART is a getty console, not a modem-line loopback -- so that half stays
        bench/driver-termios scope; the wire path verifies the firmware's
        flow-mode *policy* only.

        Observed: the hub ACCEPTs the write with LSTP_SUCCESS and the flow nibble
        mutates to the requested mode (read-back != NONE) -- it validates neither
        ``data_bits`` (UART-004) nor ``flow`` even though it validates
        ``stop_bits`` (UART-007). That is neither rejection nor ignore, so the
        spec-correct assertion xfails on finding F12. Note the mutation is also
        one-way in-band: once flow is non-zero, writing the nibble back to 0 is
        ACKed but does not latch (a flow write of 0 reads as "no change"), so
        ``config_restored`` cannot clear it and warns -- only the VOLATILE
        power-cycle revert restores NONE. The channel still transmits meanwhile
        (there are no hardware flow lines to gate it), which is asserted below.
        """
        cid = uart_channel.ch_id
        softloop.flush_rx(wire_transport, cid)
        with ch0.config_restored(wire_transport, cid) as snap:
            if len(snap.config) < uart.CONFIG_SIZE:
                pytest.skip("UART channel exposes no writable config body")
            orig = bytes(snap.config)
            baseline = uart.read_config(wire_transport, cid).flow
            # Full-body write with the flow nibble (parity_flow[7:4], offset 6) set
            # to an unsupported mode; keep the parity nibble untouched.
            bad = bytearray(orig)
            bad[6] = (bad[6] & 0x0F) | (int(mode) << 4)
            status, _ = ch0.request_write_body(wire_transport, cid, bytes(bad), offset=0)
            after = uart.read_config(wire_transport, cid)
            accepted = status == proto.Status.SUCCESS
            ignored = after.flow == baseline
            if accepted and not ignored:
                deviations.xfail(
                    "finding F12: unsupported UART flow mode "
                    f"{uart.Flow(mode).name} accepted / config mutated "
                    f"(status=SUCCESS, flow->{after.flow}); SADD UART-005 requires "
                    "unsupported flow modes to be rejected or ignored (flow stays "
                    "NONE), not latched"
                )
            # Passing shape: either the device rejected the write (and left the
            # config unchanged) or it accepted but ignored the field (flow==NONE).
            if not accepted:
                assert after.flow == baseline, "flow mode changed despite a rejected write"
            assert after.flow == baseline, (
                f"flow mode latched to {after.flow} (expected it to stay {baseline})"
            )
        # Channel still transmits after restore (printable, never submitted).
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)
        status, _ = uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, softloop.printable(8))
        assert status == proto.Status.SUCCESS
        softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)


class TestUartSoak:
    @pytest.mark.slow
    def test_loopback_soak(self, wire_transport, uart_loopback, stress_iters, soak_seconds):
        """UART-009 (partial): repeated printable loopback stays byte-for-byte.

        A compact stand-in for the 1-hour bidirectional soak: a rotating printable
        payload, each iteration verified through the safe soft loopback. Two
        sizings -- by default ``min(stress_iters, 100)`` iterations; when
        ``--soak-seconds`` is set the loop instead runs for that wall-clock
        duration (e.g. ``--soak-seconds 720`` for 20% of the SADD 1-hour mandate).
        The per-baud sweep, binary payloads and memory/queue-leak checks stay in
        the driver soak suite -- this rig's UART is a single-baud getty console.
        """
        cid = uart_loopback.ch_id
        deadline = time.monotonic() + soak_seconds if soak_seconds else None
        iters = min(stress_iters, 100)
        i = 0
        while (time.monotonic() < deadline) if deadline is not None else (i < iters):
            payload = softloop.printable(16, seed=i)
            echoed = _loopback(wire_transport, uart_loopback, payload, timeout_ms=2000)
            assert echoed == payload, f"iter {i}: {echoed!r} != {payload!r}"
            i += 1
        if not uart_loopback.binary_safe:
            softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)

def _add(parser, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
    """addoption that tolerates the parent suite already registering it."""
    try:
        parser.addoption(*args, **kwargs)
    except ValueError:
        pass


def pytest_configure(config):
    global _config
    _config = config
    for marker in (
        "transport(name): wire transport this test targets (libusb)",
        "target(name): device under test (real, emulated)",
        "faults: device->host fault injection (requires the emulated target)",
        "destructive: mutates persistent/OTP device state; needs --allow-destructive",
        "slow: long-running (soak/stress) test",
        "stress: high-volume stress/fuzz test",
    ):
        config.addinivalue_line("markers", marker)

def pytest_terminal_summary(terminalreporter, exitstatus, config):
    """Summarise the target's deviations: what is accepted, what is still broken.

    A plain xfail count cannot answer the question that matters while a part is
    stabilising -- how many of these are waivers and how many are open defects
    riding along so CI stays unblocked -- so spell it out, and flag declarations
    this run never reproduced as candidates for deletion.
    """
    import deviations

    rows = deviations.report_rows()
    if not rows:
        return

    tr = terminalreporter
    tr.write_sep("=", f"LSTP deviations: {deviations.target()}")
    for row in rows:
        mark = "seen" if row["observed"] else "not seen"
        ticket = f" [{row['ticket']}]" if row["ticket"] else ""
        tr.write_line(
            "  %-5s %-11s %-9s %s%s"
            % (row["finding"], row["status"], mark, row["note"][:88], ticket)
        )

    opens = [r for r in rows if r["status"] == deviations.OPEN]
    accepted = [r for r in rows if r["status"] == deviations.ACCEPTED]
    undeclared = deviations.undeclared_ids()
    tr.write_line(
        "  totals: %d open defect(s) xfailed, %d accepted waiver(s), %d undeclared"
        % (len(opens), len(accepted), len(undeclared))
    )
    if undeclared:
        tr.write_line(
            "  UNDECLARED (hard failures): %s -- triage, then declare or fix"
            % ", ".join(undeclared)
        )
    stale = deviations.unobserved_ids()
    if stale:
        tr.write_line(
            "  never reproduced this run: %s -- either the covering test did not "
            "run (marker/layout skip), or the device no longer deviates and the "
            "declaration should be deleted" % ", ".join(stale)
        )

    dest = config.getoption("--deviations-report", default=None)
    if dest:
        import json

        payload = {
            "target": deviations.target(),
            "exitstatus": int(exitstatus),
            "findings": list(rows),
        }
        with open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(payload, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
        tr.write_line(f"  deviation record written to {dest}")

def _select_interface(tr, interfaces, usb_path_opt):
    """Pick one LSTP interface, honoring ``--usb-path`` (sysfs basename) selection.

    Without ``--usb-path``: return the sole interface, or skip when several are
    present (ambiguous, no way to choose). With ``--usb-path`` -- e.g.
    ``1-1.1.5`` or ``1-1.1.5:1.0`` (the ``:config.intf`` suffix is ignored) --
    return the interface on the device whose sysfs ``<bus>-<port...>`` basename
    matches, and raise ``UsageError`` when it matches none or is ambiguous, so a
    stale/typo'd path fails loudly instead of silently opening the wrong DUT.
    """
    if usb_path_opt:
        want = usb_path_opt.split(":", 1)[0]
        named = [(tr.sysfs_usb_name(i.device), i) for i in interfaces]
        matches = [i for name, i in named if name == want]
        avail = ", ".join(sorted(n for n, _ in named if n)) or "(none)"
        if not matches:
            raise pytest.UsageError(
                f"--usb-path {usb_path_opt!r} matched no LSTP device (available: {avail})"
            )
        if len(matches) > 1:
            raise pytest.UsageError(
                f"--usb-path {usb_path_opt!r} is ambiguous ({len(matches)} matching "
                "LSTP interfaces)"
            )
        return matches[0]
    if len(interfaces) > 1:
        avail = (
            ", ".join(sorted(n for n in (tr.sysfs_usb_name(i.device) for i in interfaces) if n))
            or "(unknown)"
        )
        pytest.skip(f"{len(interfaces)} LSTP interfaces found ({avail}); pass --usb-path to select")
    return interfaces[0]

@pytest.fixture(scope="session", autouse=True)
def wire_volatile_mode(wire_transport, request):
    """Put the device in VOLATILE (To-RAM) config mode for the whole wire session.

    This is the single, authoritative "make writes non-destructive" step: every
    WRITE_CONFIG issued anywhere in the session lands in RAM only, so nothing is
    written to Flash/OTP and a power cycle fully reverts any config mutation.
    Set once up front (and verified by read-back so a device that refuses is
    surfaced immediately rather than silently persisting writes), then the entry
    mode is restored at session teardown. Per-test ``ch0.config_restored`` also
    requests VOLATILE, which is a no-op while this session default is in effect.

    Yields ``None`` instead of failing when the device cannot be put in VOLATILE
    -- either it does not implement READ/WRITE_CONFIG_MODE, or it answers the
    switch with an error (some targets support only the To-Flash default). That is
    a per-device capability, not a suite error: aborting the session here would
    take down every read-only and data-path test too. Config writes then guard
    themselves instead -- :func:`ops.ch0.config_restored` skips unless VOLATILE is
    verified, and the few tests that write a descriptor directly take the
    ``volatile_writes`` fixture -- so nothing can land in Flash/OTP unnoticed.
    Never writes FUSED_LOCKED.

    So when VOLATILE cannot be set, every config-write test skips and nothing can
    land in Flash/OTP -- but the skip is per write site rather than session-wide,
    because this fixture is session-scoped and autouse: skipping in here would
    take the read-only, discovery and data-path tests down with it, which on a
    part that has no To-RAM mode at all is the whole suite.

    A board YAML may set ``UNSAFE_ignore_write_config_mode_result: true`` to run
    the config-write tests anyway on a target that refuses the mode switch. That
    accepts possibly-persistent (Flash/OTP) writes, so it is only for bringup /
    development silicon -- never a production part.
    """
    import warnings

    import lstp_proto as proto
    from ops import ch0

    board = request.config.getoption("--board", default=None)
    cfg = read_board_cfg(board) if board else None
    unsafe = bool((cfg or {}).get("UNSAFE_ignore_write_config_mode_result", False))
    ch0.IGNORE_CONFIG_MODE_RESULT = unsafe

    entry = ch0.read_config_mode(wire_transport)
    if entry is None:
        warnings.warn(
            "device does not report a config mode (READ_CONFIG_MODE); config "
            "writes cannot be forced To-RAM -- treating write tests as potentially "
            "persistent.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        yield None
        return

    switched = False
    if entry != proto.ConfigMode.VOLATILE:
        status = ch0.write_config_mode(wire_transport, proto.ConfigMode.VOLATILE)
        got = ch0.read_config_mode(wire_transport)
        switched = status == proto.Status.SUCCESS and got == proto.ConfigMode.VOLATILE
        if not switched:
            warnings.warn(
                "device refused VOLATILE config mode (WRITE_CONFIG_MODE "
                f"status={proto.Status(status).name}, still {got!r}); config-write "
                "tests "
                + (
                    "RUN ANYWAY and may persist to Flash/OTP because the board "
                    "YAML sets UNSAFE_ignore_write_config_mode_result."
                    if unsafe
                    else "skip rather than risk a persistent Flash/OTP write."
                )
                + " Read-only and data-path tests are unaffected.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            yield entry if unsafe else None
            return
    try:
        yield proto.ConfigMode.VOLATILE
    finally:
        if switched:
            # A test may have left unsolicited traffic in the bulk-IN pipe (e.g.
            # asynchronous UART console echo from a soak); drain it so this
            # restore reads its own response rather than a stale frame.
            wire_transport.drain()
            ch0.write_config_mode(wire_transport, entry)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UartLoopback:
    """A confirmed UART echo path.

    ``binary_safe`` is True only when ``--uart-loopback-raw`` asserts a real
    hardware TX<->RX short (no console on the line); otherwise the peer is a
    live serial console driven as a printable-only *soft* loopback.
    """

    ch_id: int
    binary_safe: bool


@pytest.fixture
def uart_loopback(request, wire_transport, uart_channel):
    """Confirm the UART TX->RX path echoes, and return a :class:`UartLoopback`.

    Default (soft) path: the far end is treated as a live serial console. The
    fixture drives it *safely* via :mod:`softloop` -- it clears the console line
    with Ctrl-U (VKILL), never transmits CR/LF (so nothing is ever submitted to
    the login), and requires a printable nonce back byte-for-byte. No getty or
    system state is touched. Skips when no echo path is present so a layout
    without UART loopback still collects cleanly.

    Raw path (``--uart-loopback-raw``): the operator asserts a real hardware
    short, so a full-range *binary* nonce is required back and ``binary_safe``
    is set, unlocking byte-exact binary loopback tests.
    """
    import os

    import lstp_proto as proto
    import softloop
    from ops import uart

    cid = uart_channel.ch_id
    raw = bool(request.config.getoption("--uart-loopback-raw", default=False))

    if raw:
        # Real hardware short: drain, then require a full-range binary nonce back.
        wire_transport.drain(timeout_ms=100)
        nonce = os.urandom(32)
        uart.request_write(wire_transport, cid, nonce)
        got = uart.read_rx_until(wire_transport, cid, len(nonce), timeout_ms=1500)
        if got.data != nonce:
            pytest.skip(
                "--uart-loopback-raw set but TX/RX is not a byte-exact binary "
                "loopback (is a hardware short actually fitted?)"
            )
        return UartLoopback(ch_id=cid, binary_safe=True)

    # Soft path: printable-only nonce via the console peer, Ctrl-U bracketed.
    nonce = softloop.printable(16, seed=os.urandom(1)[0])
    echoed = softloop.soft_loopback(wire_transport, cid, nonce, timeout_ms=1500)
    softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid)
    if echoed != nonce:
        pytest.skip("UART peer is not a byte-exact echo path for printable data")
    # Best-effort at teardown: raising from a finalizer would mask whatever the
    # test was actually reporting.
    request.addfinalizer(lambda: softloop.clear_line(wire_transport, cid, strict=False))
    return UartLoopback(ch_id=cid, binary_safe=False)


# EEPROM write page size (bytes) implied by the AT24Cxx family type string in
# the board YAML ``i2c_eeprom`` map. A single WRITE never crosses a page, so the
# integrity tests derive the write granularity from the declared chip type
# instead of hard-coding it. Falls back to the smallest common page (8) for an
# unknown type.
_EEPROM_PAGE_BY_TYPE = {
    "24c01": 8,
    "24c02": 8,
    "24c04": 16,
    "24c08": 16,
    "24c16": 16,
    "24c32": 32,
    "24c64": 32,
    "24c128": 64,
    "24c256": 64,
    "24c512": 128,
}


def _eeprom_page_for(type_str: str) -> int:
    return _EEPROM_PAGE_BY_TYPE.get(str(type_str).strip().lower(), 8)
